nodes.name: TMRCA and total branch length orders of SMC genealogies
nodes.statement: \citet{jacob2015} showed that the TMRCA and total branch length of all $N$ particles are both $O( N \log N )$, while \cite{koskela2020annals} showed that those for a sample of $n$ particles are $\Theta( N )$ and $\Theta( N \log n )$, respectively, strongly suggesting that the results of \citet{jacob2015} could be sharpened to $\Theta(N)$ and $\Theta(N \log N)$, respectively.

nodes.name: n-coalescent
nodes.statement: The \emph{$n$-coalescent} \citep{kingman1982coal, kingman1982exch,kingman1982gene} is a homogeneous continuous-time Markov process on the space $\mathcal{P}_n$ of partitions of $\{1,\dots,n\} =: [ n ]$.
differentia: on the space $\mathcal{P}_n$ of partitions of $\{1,\dots,n\} =: [ n ]$

nodes.name: Generator of the n-coalescent
nodes.statement: The non-zero entries of its infinitesimal generator $Q$ are \begin{equation*} q_{\xi,\eta} = \begin{cases} -|\xi|(|\xi|-1)/2 & \xi=\eta \\ 1 & \xi \prec \eta \end{cases} \end{equation*} for every $\xi, \eta \in \mathcal{P}_n$, where $|\xi|$ denotes the number of blocks in $\xi$, and $\xi \prec \eta$ means that $\eta$ is obtained from $\xi$ by merging exactly two blocks.
nodes.statement_short: Generator Q of the n-coalescent: rate 1 for each pair merger, diagonal $-|\xi|(|\xi|-1)/2$.

nodes.name: Interacting particle system
nodes.statement: Consider an interacting particle system in which $N$ particles stochastically reproduce in discrete, non-overlapping generations, such that each particle in generation $t \in \mathbb{N}$ has a single parent in the previous generation.

nodes.name: Parental indices and offspring counts
nodes.statement: The index of the generation-$t$ parent of individual $j$ in generation $t - 1$ is denoted $a_t^{(j)} \in [N]$, and the number of offspring that individual $i$ in generation $t$ has in generation $t-1$ is $\nu_t^{(i)} := |\{ j: a_t^{(j)} = i \}|$.

nodes.name: Genealogical process
nodes.statement: In particular, sample $n\leq N$ individuals from generation $0$ uniformly without replacement, and trace back the corresponding lineages to obtain their genealogy which, following \citet{kingman1982coal}, is encoded by a $\mathcal{P}_n$-valued stochastic process $(G_t^{(n,N)})_{t\in\mathbb{N}}$ with initial value $G_0^{(n,N)} = \{ \{1\}, \dots, \{n\} \} =: \Delta $. At each $t\in\mathbb{N}$, two indices $i\neq j \in [n]$ are in the same block of $G_t^{(n,N)}$ if and only if terminal particles $i$ and $j$ share a common ancestor at time $t$ (i.e.\ $t$ generations back).
nodes.statement_short: The genealogy of n sampled terminal particles as a partition-valued process; i,j share a block iff they share an ancestor t generations back.

nodes.name: Random assignment condition (A1)
nodes.statement: The conditional distribution of parental indices $a_t^{(1:N)}$ given offspring counts $\nu_t^{(1:N)}$ is uniform over all assignments such that $ |\{ j: a_t^{(j)} =i \}|= \nu_t^{(i)} $ for all $i$.
nodes.statement_short: Given offspring counts, parental indices are assigned uniformly at random.

nodes.name: Conditional pair merger probability
nodes.statement: To define this time scale, we first define the conditional pair merger probability, \begin{equation} c_N(t) := \frac{1}{(N)_2} \sum_{i=1}^N (\nu_t^{(i)})_2, \end{equation} where $(n)_k := n (n - 1) \cdots (n - k + 1)$ is the falling factorial.

nodes.name: Time scale tau_N
nodes.statement: To achieve a limiting pair merger rate of 1, as in the $n$-coalescent, we rescale time by the left-inverse: \begin{equation} \tau_N(t) := \inf \left\{ s \in \mathbb{N} : \sum_{r=1}^s c_N(r) \geq t \right\} . \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Random time change: tau_N(t) is the first generation where the cumulative pair-merger probability reaches t.

nodes.name: Definition of tau_N
nodes.statement: \tau_N(t) := \inf \left\{ s \in \mathbb{N} : \sum_{r=1}^s c_N(r) \geq t \right\} .
nodes.label: eq:defn_tauN

nodes.name: Random versus deterministic time scale
nodes.statement: Our definition of $c_N(t)$ differs from that which is usual in the population genetics literature, where the deterministic function defined as the expectation of \eqref{eq:defn_cN} is identified as $c_N(t)$. Our definition yields a time scale which is random, depending on the realisation of $\nu_t^{(1:N)}$ for each $t$. In the context of SMC, this is necessary to accommodate the heterogeneity of the system: the random time scale subsumes the time-inhomogeneity of the model, so that the rescaled ancestry converges to a time homogeneous process. Inhomogeneous time scales have been studied in the genetics context as models of variable population size, but even in these settings $c_N(t)$ is defined as an expectation so that the inhomogeneous time scale varies deterministically \citep{mohle2002coal}.
nodes.statement_short: Unlike population genetics, c_N(t) is random (not an expectation), so the time scale absorbs SMC time-inhomogeneity.

nodes.statement: For all $t\in\mathbb{N}$, $t^\prime > s^\prime \geq 0$, \begin{enumerate}[label=$(\alph*)$] \item \hspace{5pt} $\begin{aligned} 0 \leq D_N(t) \leq c_N(t) \leq 1, \end{aligned}$ \item \hspace{5pt} $\begin{aligned} t^\prime - (s^\prime + 1) \mathds{1}_{ ( 0, \infty ) }( s^\prime ) \leq \sum_{r=\tau_N(s^\prime) + 1}^{\tau_N(t^\prime)} c_N(r) \leq t^\prime +1, \end{aligned}$ \item \hspace{5pt} $\begin{aligned} \tau_N(t^\prime) \geq t^\prime. \end{aligned}$ \end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Naturalness of the merger-ratio condition
nodes.statement: Condition \eqref{eq:mainthmcondition2} is very natural: it requires the rate of (combinations of) mergers involving three or more lineages to be vanishingly small in comparison to that of binary mergers. The sequence $( b_N )_{ N \in \mathbb{N} }$ controls the rate at which the ratio of rates of large and binary mergers vanishes, and can decay to zero arbitrarily slowly. The exact values of its entries are not special; it is just the sequence that plays an implicit role in the usual little-o notation. As mentioned in Section \ref{sec:intro}, a natural analogue of \eqref{eq:mainthmcondition2} is known to be necessary and sufficient for convergence to the $n$-coalescent in the neutral case \citep[Equation (16)]{mohle2000}.
nodes.statement_short: The condition asks triple-or-larger mergers to be negligible relative to binary ones; its neutral analogue is necessary and sufficient.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1
nodes.statement: The structure of the proof follows \citet{mohle1999}, albeit with considerable technical complication due to the dependence between generations (non-neutrality) in our model. To make it digestible, the proof is broken down into a number of results which are organised into sections; the relationships between these are shown in Figure~\ref{fig:weakconv_structure}. Convergence of the finite-dimensional distributions was proved in \citet[Theorem 3.2]{brown2021}. Strengthening this to weak convergence on the space of processes amounts to establishing relative compactness of the sequence $\{ (G_{\tau_N(t)}^{(n,N)})_{t\geq0} \}_{N\in\mathbb{N}}$. Since $\mathcal{P}_n$ is finite and therefore complete and separable, and the sample paths of $(G_{\tau_N(t)}^{(n,N)})_{t\geq0}$ live in $\mathcal{D}$, we can apply \citet[Chapter 3, Corollary 7.4]{ethier1986} which states that a sequence of processes $\{ (G_{\tau_N(t)}^{(n,N)})_{t\geq0} \}_{N\in\mathbb{N}}$ is relatively compact if and only if the following two conditions hold: \begin{enumerate} \item For every $\epsilon>0$ and rational $t\geq 0$, there exists a compact set $\Gamma_{ \epsilon, t } \subseteq \mathcal{P}_n$ such that \begin{equation*} \liminf_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{P}\left[ G_{\tau_N(t)}^{(n,N)} \in \Gamma_{ \epsilon, t } \right] \geq 1-\epsilon. \end{equation*} \item For every $\epsilon>0$, $t>0$ there exists $\delta>0$ such that \begin{equation} \liminf_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{P}\left[ \omega\left( G_{\tau_N(\cdot)}^{(n,N)}, \delta, t \right) < \epsilon \right] \geq 1-\epsilon, \end{equation} where $\omega$ is the modified modulus of continuity: \begin{equation*} \omega\left( G_{\tau_N(\cdot)}^{(n,N)}, \delta, t \right) := \inf \max_{i \in [K]} \sup_{u,v \in [T_{i-1}, T_i)} \rho\left( G_{\tau_N(u)}^{(n,N)}, G_{\tau_N(v)}^{(n,N)} \right), \end{equation*} with the infimum taken over all partitions of the form $0=T_0<T_1<\cdots <T_{K-1} <t \leq T_K$ (for any $K$) such that $\min_{i\in[K]} (T_i - T_{i-1}) > \delta$. \end{enumerate} Since $\mathcal{P}_n$ is finite and hence compact, Condition~\ref{item:relcomp1} is satisfied automatically with $\Gamma_{ \epsilon, t } = \mathcal{P}_n$. Intuitively, Condition~\ref{item:relcomp2} ensures that the jumps of the process are well-separated. In our case, $\rho( G_{\tau_N(u)}^{(n,N)}, G_{\tau_N(v)}^{(n,N)} ) = 1$ if there is at least one jump between times $u$ and $v$, and 0 otherwise. The supremum and maximum indicate whether there is a jump inside any of the intervals of the given partition; this can be zero only if all of the jumps up to time $t$ occur exactly at the times $T_{ 0 : K }$. The infimum over all allowed partitions can only equal zero if no two jumps occur less than $\delta$ (unscaled) time apart. To prove Theorem \ref{thm:weakconv}, it remains to verify Condition \ref{item:relcomp2}. To do this, we use a coupling with a process for which Condition \ref{item:relcomp2} is easier to check, and which will imply that it also holds for the genealogical process of interest. Define $p_t := \max_{\xi\in \mathcal{P}_n} \{1 - p_{\xi\xi}(t)\} = 1 - p_{\Delta\Delta}(t)$, where $\Delta = \{ \{1\},\dots, \{n\} \}$. For a proof that the maximum is attained at $\xi = \Delta$, see Lemma~\ref{thm:maximum_pr}. Following \citet{mohle1999}, we construct the process $(Z_t, S_t)_{t \in \mathbb{N}_0}$ on $\mathbb{N}_0 \times \mathcal{P}_n$ with initial state $( Z_0, S_0 ) = ( 0, \Delta )$, and conditional transition probabilities \begin{align} \mathbb{P}[ Z_t = j , S_t = \eta \mid& Z_{t-1} = i, S_{t-1} = \xi, \mathcal{F}_\infty ] \notag\\ &= \begin{cases} 1 - p_t &\quad \text{if } j=i \text{ and } \eta=\xi, \\ p_{\xi\xi}(t) + p_t - 1 &\quad \text{if } j=i+1 \text{ and } \eta=\xi, \\ p_{\xi\eta}(t) &\quad \text{if } j=i+1 \text{ and } \eta\neq\xi, \\ 0 &\quad \text{otherwise}. \end{cases} \end{align} The definition of $p_t$ ensures that the second case of \eqref{eq:constructed_chain} is non-negative, attaining the value zero when $\xi=\Delta$. Unlike the corresponding process in \citet{mohle1999}, the transition probabilities in \eqref{eq:constructed_chain} depend on offspring counts. Thus, $(Z_t, S_t)$ is only Markovian conditional on $\mathcal{F}_\infty$, and can be thought of as a time-inhomogeneous Markov chain in a random environment. Marginally, $(S_t)$ has the same distribution as the genealogical process of interest, while $(Z_t)$ jumps whenever $(S_t)$ does, but also has some extra jumps. The jump times of $(Z_t)$ do not depend on the current state, making it much easier to analyse. Our construction also resembles that of \citet{mohle2002coal}, where the process $(S_t)$ is also time-inhomogeneous but still Markovian without conditioning on a random environment. The coupling of jumps implies that the modulus of continuity of $(Z_t)$ is at least as large as that of $(S_t)$. Hence, we will show that \eqref{modulus_of_continuity} holds for $(Z_t)$, and conclude that it also holds for the genealogical processes of interest. Denote by $0=T_0^{(N)}<T_1^{(N)}<\dots$ the jump times of the rescaled process $(Z_{\tau_N(t)})_{t\geq0}$, and by $\varpi_i^{(N)} := T_i^{(N)} - T_{i-1}^{(N)}$ the corresponding holding times. Suppose that for some fixed $\varpi_1^{(N)}, \varpi_2^{(N)}, \dots$ and $t>0$, there exists $m \in \mathbb{N}$ and $\delta >0$ such that $\varpi_i^{(N)} > \delta$ for all $i\in [m]$, and $T_m^{(N)} \geq t$. Then $K_N := \min\{i : T_i^{(N)} \geq t\}$ is well-defined with $1\leq K_N \leq m$, and $T_{ 1 : K_N }^{(N)}$ is a partition of the form required for Condition~\ref{item:relcomp2}. Indeed $(Z_{\tau_N(\cdot)})$ is constant on every interval $[ T_{i-1}^{(N)} , T_i^{(N)} )$ by construction, so $\omega( (Z_{\tau_N(\cdot))} , \delta, t ) = 0$. We therefore have that for each $m \in \mathbb{N}$ and $\delta >0$, \begin{equation*} \mathbb{P}\left[ \omega\left( (Z_{\tau_N(\cdot)}) , \delta, t \right) < \epsilon \right] \geq \mathbb{P}\left[ T_m^{(N)} \geq t, \varpi_i^{(N)} > \delta \,\forall i\in [m] \right] . \end{equation*} Thus, a sufficient condition for Condition~\ref{item:relcomp2} to hold is: for any $\epsilon>0$, $t>0$, there exist $m\in\mathbb{N}$, $\delta>0$ such that \begin{equation} \liminf_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{P}\left[ T_m^{(N)} \geq t, \varpi_i^{(N)} > \delta \,\forall i\in [m]\right] \geq 1-\epsilon . \end{equation} By Lemma~\ref{thm:holdingtimes_distn}, below, the limiting distributions of $\varpi_i^{(N)}$ are i.i.d.\ $\operatorname{Exp}(\alpha_n)$, where $\alpha_n := n(n-1)/2$, so \begin{equation*} \limsup_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{P}\left[ \varpi_i^{(N)} \leq \delta \right] = 1- \liminf_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{P}\left[ \varpi_i^{(N)} > \delta \right] = 1- e^{-\alpha_n \delta} \end{equation*} for each $i$, and \begin{align*} \limsup_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{P}\left[ T_m^{(N)} < t \right] &= 1- \liminf_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{P}\left[ T_m^{(N)} \geq t \right] \\ &= 1- \liminf_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{P}\left[ \varpi_1^{(N)} + \cdots + \varpi_m^{(N)} \geq t \right] \\ &= 1- e^{-\alpha_n t} \sum_{i=0}^{m-1} \frac{(\alpha_n t)^i}{i!}, \end{align*} using the series expansion for the Erlang CDF \citep[see for example][Chapter 15]{forbes2011}. Now \begin{align*} \liminf_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{P}[ T_m^{(N)} \geq t, &\varpi_i^{(N)} > \delta \,\forall i\in [m] ] \\ &\geq 1 - \limsup_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{P}\left[ T_m^{(N)} < t \right] - \sum_{i=1}^m \limsup_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{P}\left[ \varpi_i^{(N)} \leq \delta\right]\\ &= 1- \Bigg( 1- e^{-\alpha_n t} \sum_{i=0}^{m-1} \frac{(\alpha_n t)^i}{i!} \Bigg) - m( 1- e^{-\alpha_n \delta} ) , \end{align*} which can be made $\geq 1-\epsilon$ by taking $m$ sufficiently large and $\delta$ sufficiently small. Since this argument applies for any $\epsilon$ and $t$, \eqref{eq:condition2b} is satisfied. Hence, so is Condition~\ref{item:relcomp2}, and the proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Relative compactness via Ethier-Kurtz modulus-of-continuity criterion, checked on a coupled jump process (Z_t,S_t). The key step is that holding times of Z converge to i.i.d. Exp(alpha_n) (Lemma 2).

nodes.name: Relative compactness criterion in Skorokhod space
nodes.statement: Since $\mathcal{P}_n$ is finite and therefore complete and separable, and the sample paths of $(G_{\tau_N(t)}^{(n,N)})_{t\geq0}$ live in $\mathcal{D}$, we can apply \citet[Chapter 3, Corollary 7.4]{ethier1986} which states that a sequence of processes $\{ (G_{\tau_N(t)}^{(n,N)})_{t\geq0} \}_{N\in\mathbb{N}}$ is relatively compact if and only if the following two conditions hold: \begin{enumerate} \item For every $\epsilon>0$ and rational $t\geq 0$, there exists a compact set $\Gamma_{ \epsilon, t } \subseteq \mathcal{P}_n$ such that \begin{equation*} \liminf_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{P}\left[ G_{\tau_N(t)}^{(n,N)} \in \Gamma_{ \epsilon, t } \right] \geq 1-\epsilon. \end{equation*} \item For every $\epsilon>0$, $t>0$ there exists $\delta>0$ such that \begin{equation} \liminf_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{P}\left[ \omega\left( G_{\tau_N(\cdot)}^{(n,N)}, \delta, t \right) < \epsilon \right] \geq 1-\epsilon, \end{equation} where $\omega$ is the modified modulus of continuity: \begin{equation*} \omega\left( G_{\tau_N(\cdot)}^{(n,N)}, \delta, t \right) := \inf \max_{i \in [K]} \sup_{u,v \in [T_{i-1}, T_i)} \rho\left( G_{\tau_N(u)}^{(n,N)}, G_{\tau_N(v)}^{(n,N)} \right), \end{equation*} with the infimum taken over all partitions of the form $0=T_0<T_1<\cdots <T_{K-1} <t \leq T_K$ (for any $K$) such that $\min_{i\in[K]} (T_i - T_{i-1}) > \delta$.
conclusions: a sequence of processes $\{ (G_{\tau_N(t)}^{(n,N)})_{t\geq0} \}_{N\in\mathbb{N}}$ is relatively compact if and only if the following two conditions hold
equivalent_conditions: a sequence of processes $\{ (G_{\tau_N(t)}^{(n,N)})_{t\geq0} \}_{N\in\mathbb{N}}$ is relatively compact
nodes.statement_short: A sequence of cadlag processes on a complete separable space is relatively compact iff compact containment and a modulus-of-continuity condition hold.

nodes.name: Modulus of continuity condition
nodes.statement: \liminf_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{P}\left[ \omega\left( G_{\tau_N(\cdot)}^{(n,N)}, \delta, t \right) < \epsilon \right] \geq 1-\epsilon,
nodes.label: modulus_of_continuity

nodes.name: Transition probabilities of the coupled process (Z_t,S_t)
nodes.statement: \mathbb{P}[ Z_t = j , S_t = \eta \mid& Z_{t-1} = i, S_{t-1} = \xi, \mathcal{F}_\infty ] \notag\\ &= \begin{cases} 1 - p_t &\quad \text{if } j=i \text{ and } \eta=\xi, \\ p_{\xi\xi}(t) + p_t - 1 &\quad \text{if } j=i+1 \text{ and } \eta=\xi, \\ p_{\xi\eta}(t) &\quad \text{if } j=i+1 \text{ and } \eta\neq\xi, \\ 0 &\quad \text{otherwise}. \end{cases}
nodes.label: eq:constructed_chain

nodes.name: Sufficient condition on jump and holding times
nodes.statement: \liminf_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{P}\left[ T_m^{(N)} \geq t, \varpi_i^{(N)} > \delta \,\forall i\in [m]\right] \geq 1-\epsilon .
nodes.label: eq:condition2b

nodes.name: proof outline
nodes.statement: The structure of the proof follows \citet{mohle1999}, albeit with considerable technical complication due to the dependence between generations (non-neutrality) in our model. To make it digestible, the proof is broken down into a number of results which are organised into sections; the relationships between these are shown in Figure~\ref{fig:weakconv_structure}.
nodes.statement_short: Proof follows Mohle (1999), split into results

nodes.name: reduce to relative compactness
nodes.statement: Convergence of the finite-dimensional distributions was proved in \citet[Theorem 3.2]{brown2021}. Strengthening this to weak convergence on the space of processes amounts to establishing relative compactness of the sequence $\{ (G_{\tau_N(t)}^{(n,N)})_{t\geq0} \}_{N\in\mathbb{N}}$. Since $\mathcal{P}_n$ is finite and therefore complete and separable, and the sample paths of $(G_{\tau_N(t)}^{(n,N)})_{t\geq0}$ live in $\mathcal{D}$, we can apply \citet[Chapter 3, Corollary 7.4]{ethier1986} which states that a sequence of processes $\{ (G_{\tau_N(t)}^{(n,N)})_{t\geq0} \}_{N\in\mathbb{N}}$ is relatively compact if and only if the following two conditions hold: \begin{enumerate} \item For every $\epsilon>0$ and rational $t\geq 0$, there exists a compact set $\Gamma_{ \epsilon, t } \subseteq \mathcal{P}_n$ such that \begin{equation*} \liminf_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{P}\left[ G_{\tau_N(t)}^{(n,N)} \in \Gamma_{ \epsilon, t } \right] \geq 1-\epsilon. \end{equation*} \item For every $\epsilon>0$, $t>0$ there exists $\delta>0$ such that \begin{equation} \liminf_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{P}\left[ \omega\left( G_{\tau_N(\cdot)}^{(n,N)}, \delta, t \right) < \epsilon \right] \geq 1-\epsilon, \end{equation} where $\omega$ is the modified modulus of continuity: \begin{equation*} \omega\left( G_{\tau_N(\cdot)}^{(n,N)}, \delta, t \right) := \inf \max_{i \in [K]} \sup_{u,v \in [T_{i-1}, T_i)} \rho\left( G_{\tau_N(u)}^{(n,N)}, G_{\tau_N(v)}^{(n,N)} \right), \end{equation*} with the infimum taken over all partitions of the form $0=T_0<T_1<\cdots <T_{K-1} <t \leq T_K$ (for any $K$) such that $\min_{i\in[K]} (T_i - T_{i-1}) > \delta$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Fdd convergence known; reduce to relative compactness via Ethier-Kurtz criterion

nodes.name: condition 1 automatic
nodes.statement: Since $\mathcal{P}_n$ is finite and hence compact, Condition~\ref{item:relcomp1} is satisfied automatically with $\Gamma_{ \epsilon, t } = \mathcal{P}_n$.
nodes.statement_short: Compact containment holds since P_n is finite

nodes.name: interpret condition 2
nodes.statement: Intuitively, Condition~\ref{item:relcomp2} ensures that the jumps of the process are well-separated. In our case, $\rho( G_{\tau_N(u)}^{(n,N)}, G_{\tau_N(v)}^{(n,N)} ) = 1$ if there is at least one jump between times $u$ and $v$, and 0 otherwise. The supremum and maximum indicate whether there is a jump inside any of the intervals of the given partition; this can be zero only if all of the jumps up to time $t$ occur exactly at the times $T_{ 0 : K }$. The infimum over all allowed partitions can only equal zero if no two jumps occur less than $\delta$ (unscaled) time apart.
nodes.statement_short: Condition 2 means jumps are well separated

nodes.name: plan: coupling
nodes.statement: To prove Theorem \ref{thm:weakconv}, it remains to verify Condition \ref{item:relcomp2}. To do this, we use a coupling with a process for which Condition \ref{item:relcomp2} is easier to check, and which will imply that it also holds for the genealogical process of interest.
nodes.statement_short: It remains to verify Condition 2, via a coupling

nodes.name: define p_t
nodes.statement: Define $p_t := \max_{\xi\in \mathcal{P}_n} \{1 - p_{\xi\xi}(t)\} = 1 - p_{\Delta\Delta}(t)$, where $\Delta = \{ \{1\},\dots, \{n\} \}$. For a proof that the maximum is attained at $\xi = \Delta$, see Lemma~\ref{thm:maximum_pr}.
nodes.statement_short: Define p_t as the maximal jump probability, attained at Delta

nodes.name: construct coupled chain
nodes.statement: Following \citet{mohle1999}, we construct the process $(Z_t, S_t)_{t \in \mathbb{N}_0}$ on $\mathbb{N}_0 \times \mathcal{P}_n$ with initial state $( Z_0, S_0 ) = ( 0, \Delta )$, and conditional transition probabilities \begin{align} \mathbb{P}[ Z_t = j , S_t = \eta \mid& Z_{t-1} = i, S_{t-1} = \xi, \mathcal{F}_\infty ] \notag\\ &= \begin{cases} 1 - p_t &\quad \text{if } j=i \text{ and } \eta=\xi, \\ p_{\xi\xi}(t) + p_t - 1 &\quad \text{if } j=i+1 \text{ and } \eta=\xi, \\ p_{\xi\eta}(t) &\quad \text{if } j=i+1 \text{ and } \eta\neq\xi, \\ 0 &\quad \text{otherwise}. \end{cases} \end{align} The definition of $p_t$ ensures that the second case of \eqref{eq:constructed_chain} is non-negative, attaining the value zero when $\xi=\Delta$.
nodes.statement_short: Construct the coupled process (Z_t,S_t) in a random environment

nodes.name: properties of coupling
nodes.statement: Unlike the corresponding process in \citet{mohle1999}, the transition probabilities in \eqref{eq:constructed_chain} depend on offspring counts. Thus, $(Z_t, S_t)$ is only Markovian conditional on $\mathcal{F}_\infty$, and can be thought of as a time-inhomogeneous Markov chain in a random environment. Marginally, $(S_t)$ has the same distribution as the genealogical process of interest, while $(Z_t)$ jumps whenever $(S_t)$ does, but also has some extra jumps. The jump times of $(Z_t)$ do not depend on the current state, making it much easier to analyse. Our construction also resembles that of \citet{mohle2002coal}, where the process $(S_t)$ is also time-inhomogeneous but still Markovian without conditioning on a random environment.
nodes.statement_short: S_t is the genealogy marginally; Z_t jumps whenever S_t does

nodes.name: reduce to Z_t
nodes.statement: The coupling of jumps implies that the modulus of continuity of $(Z_t)$ is at least as large as that of $(S_t)$. Hence, we will show that \eqref{modulus_of_continuity} holds for $(Z_t)$, and conclude that it also holds for the genealogical processes of interest.
nodes.statement_short: Suffices to check modulus of continuity for Z_t

nodes.name: jump and holding times
nodes.statement: Denote by $0=T_0^{(N)}<T_1^{(N)}<\dots$ the jump times of the rescaled process $(Z_{\tau_N(t)})_{t\geq0}$, and by $\varpi_i^{(N)} := T_i^{(N)} - T_{i-1}^{(N)}$ the corresponding holding times. Suppose that for some fixed $\varpi_1^{(N)}, \varpi_2^{(N)}, \dots$ and $t>0$, there exists $m \in \mathbb{N}$ and $\delta >0$ such that $\varpi_i^{(N)} > \delta$ for all $i\in [m]$, and $T_m^{(N)} \geq t$. Then $K_N := \min\{i : T_i^{(N)} \geq t\}$ is well-defined with $1\leq K_N \leq m$, and $T_{ 1 : K_N }^{(N)}$ is a partition of the form required for Condition~\ref{item:relcomp2}. Indeed $(Z_{\tau_N(\cdot)})$ is constant on every interval $[ T_{i-1}^{(N)} , T_i^{(N)} )$ by construction, so $\omega( (Z_{\tau_N(\cdot))} , \delta, t ) = 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce jump/holding times; well-separated jumps give zero modulus

nodes.name: sufficient condition
nodes.statement: We therefore have that for each $m \in \mathbb{N}$ and $\delta >0$, \begin{equation*} \mathbb{P}\left[ \omega\left( (Z_{\tau_N(\cdot)}) , \delta, t \right) < \epsilon \right] \geq \mathbb{P}\left[ T_m^{(N)} \geq t, \varpi_i^{(N)} > \delta \,\forall i\in [m] \right] . \end{equation*} Thus, a sufficient condition for Condition~\ref{item:relcomp2} to hold is: for any $\epsilon>0$, $t>0$, there exist $m\in\mathbb{N}$, $\delta>0$ such that \begin{equation} \liminf_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{P}\left[ T_m^{(N)} \geq t, \varpi_i^{(N)} > \delta \,\forall i\in [m]\right] \geq 1-\epsilon . \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Reduce Condition 2 to condition (8) on jump and holding times

nodes.name: apply holding-time limit
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{thm:holdingtimes_distn}, below, the limiting distributions of $\varpi_i^{(N)}$ are i.i.d.\ $\operatorname{Exp}(\alpha_n)$, where $\alpha_n := n(n-1)/2$, so \begin{equation*} \limsup_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{P}\left[ \varpi_i^{(N)} \leq \delta \right] = 1- \liminf_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{P}\left[ \varpi_i^{(N)} > \delta \right] = 1- e^{-\alpha_n \delta} \end{equation*} for each $i$, and \begin{align*} \limsup_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{P}\left[ T_m^{(N)} < t \right] &= 1- \liminf_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{P}\left[ T_m^{(N)} \geq t \right] \\ &= 1- \liminf_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{P}\left[ \varpi_1^{(N)} + \cdots + \varpi_m^{(N)} \geq t \right] \\ &= 1- e^{-\alpha_n t} \sum_{i=0}^{m-1} \frac{(\alpha_n t)^i}{i!}, \end{align*} using the series expansion for the Erlang CDF \citep[see for example][Chapter 15]{forbes2011}.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Lemma 2: holding times are asymptotically i.i.d. Exp(alpha_n); Erlang CDF

nodes.name: verify condition (8)
nodes.statement: Now \begin{align*} \liminf_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{P}[ T_m^{(N)} \geq t, &\varpi_i^{(N)} > \delta \,\forall i\in [m] ] \\ &\geq 1 - \limsup_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{P}\left[ T_m^{(N)} < t \right] - \sum_{i=1}^m \limsup_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{P}\left[ \varpi_i^{(N)} \leq \delta\right]\\ &= 1- \Bigg( 1- e^{-\alpha_n t} \sum_{i=0}^{m-1} \frac{(\alpha_n t)^i}{i!} \Bigg) - m( 1- e^{-\alpha_n \delta} ) , \end{align*} which can be made $\geq 1-\epsilon$ by taking $m$ sufficiently large and $\delta$ sufficiently small.
nodes.statement_short: Union bound shows (8) for large m and small delta

nodes.name: conclude
nodes.statement: Since this argument applies for any $\epsilon$ and $t$, \eqref{eq:condition2b} is satisfied. Hence, so is Condition~\ref{item:relcomp2}, and the proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Condition 2 holds; proof complete

nodes.name: Extension to multiple-merger coalescents
nodes.statement: The neutral techniques of \cite{mohle1999} have also been used to establish weak convergence of genealogical processes to more general coalescent models featuring simultaneous mergers of more than two lineages \citep{mohle2001, mohle2003, sagitov2003}. Proofs of these results invariably contain two main parts: convergence of finite-dimensional distributions (established via convergence of generators in the Markovian setting), and control of the modulus of continuity. We expect that this strategy will allow similar results for convergence of non-neutral models to multiple merger coalescents: use an approach reminiscent of \citet[Theorem 1]{koskela2020annals} to establish convergence of finite-dimensional distributions and then adapt Theorem \ref{thm:weakconv} to control the relevant modulus of continuity.
nodes.statement_short: The strategy (fdd convergence plus modulus-of-continuity control) is expected to extend to non-neutral multiple-merger limits.

nodes.name: Elementwise vector inequality
nodes.statement: Throughout the remainder of the manuscript, we write $x_{ 1 : k } \leq y_{ 1 : k }$ for vectors $x_{ 1 : k } := ( x_1, \ldots, x_k )$ and $y_{ 1 : k }$ if the inequality holds elementwise.

nodes.name: Limiting distribution of holding times
nodes.statement: Assume \eqref{eq:mainthmcondition2} holds. Then, as $N\to\infty$, the finite-dimensional distributions of $\varpi_1^{(N)} , \varpi_2^{(N)} , \dots$ converge to those of $\varpi_1, \varpi_2, \dots$, where the $\varpi_i$ are independent $\operatorname{Exp}(\alpha_n)$-distributed random variables.
conclusions: as $N\to\infty$, the finite-dimensional distributions of $\varpi_1^{(N)} , \varpi_2^{(N)} , \dots$ converge to those of $\varpi_1, \varpi_2, \dots$, where the $\varpi_i$ are independent $\operatorname{Exp}(\alpha_n)$-distributed random variables
nodes.statement_short: Holding times of the coupled jump process converge in fdd to i.i.d. Exp(alpha_n).
nodes.label: thm:holdingtimes_distn

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2
nodes.statement: For any $k \in \mathbb{N}$, there is a continuous bijection between the jump times $T_{ 1 : k }^{(N)}$ and the holding times $\varpi_{ 1 : k }^{(N)}$. Thus, convergence of $\varpi_{ 1 : k }^{(N)}$ to $\varpi_{ 1 : k }$ is equivalent to convergence of the jump times to $T_{ 1 : k }$, where $T_i := \varpi_1+\dots+\varpi_i$. We will work with the jump times, following \citet[Lemma 3.2]{mohle1999}. The idea is to prove by induction that, for any $k\in\mathbb{N}$ and $t_{ 1 : k } > 0$, \begin{equation} \lim_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{P}\left[ T_{ 1 : k }^{(N)} \leq t_{ 1 : k } \right] = \mathbb{P}[ T_{ 1 : k } \leq t_{ 1 : k } ] . \end{equation} Take the basis case $k=1$, for which $\mathbb{P}[ T_1 \leq t ] = \mathbb{P}[ \varpi_1 \leq t ] = 1 - e^{-\alpha_n t}$ and $T_1^{(N)} >t$ if and only if $( Z_{ \tau_N( t ) } )$ has no jumps up to time $t$: \begin{equation*} \mathbb{P}\left[T_1^{(N)} >t \right] = \mathbb{E}\left[ \mathbb{P}[ T_1^{(N)} >t \mid \mathcal{F}_\infty ] \right] = \mathbb{E}\Bigg[ \prod_{r=1}^{\tau_N(t)} (1-p_r) \Bigg] . \end{equation*} Lemma~\ref{thm:basis} shows that this probability converges to $e^{-\alpha_n t}$ as required. For the induction step, assume that \eqref{eq:518} holds for some $k$. We have \begin{align*} \mathbb{P}\left[ T_{ 1 : ( k + 1 ) }^{(N)} \leq t_{ 1 : ( k + 1 ) } \right] = \mathbb{P}\left[ T_{ 1 : k }^{(N)} \leq t_{ 1 : k } \right] - \mathbb{P}\left[ T_{ 1 : k }^{(N)} \leq t_{ 1 : k }, T_{k+1}^{(N)} > t_{k+1} \right]. \end{align*} The first term on the right-hand side converges to $\mathbb{P}[ T_{ 1 : k } \leq t_{ 1 : k } ]$ by the induction hypothesis, and it remains to show that \begin{align} \lim_{N\to\infty} &\mathbb{P}\left[ T_{ 1 : k }^{(N)} \leq t_{ 1 : k }, T_{k+1}^{(N)} > t_{k+1} \right] = \mathbb{P}[ T_{ 1 : k }\leq t_{ 1 : k }, T_{k+1} > t_{k+1} ]. \end{align} As shown in \citet[p.\ 459]{mohle1999}, \begin{equation*} \mathbb{P}[ T_{ 1 : k }\leq t_{ 1 : k }, T_{k+1} > t_{k+1} ] = \alpha_n^k e^{-\alpha_n t} \sum_{\substack{i_1\leq \dots\leq i_{k-1}\\ \in \{0,\dots,k\} : \\ i_j \geq j \forall j}} \prod_{j=1}^k \frac{(t_j - t_{j-1})^{i_j - i_{j-1}}}{(i_j - i_{j-1})! } , \end{equation*} while the probability on the left-hand side of \eqref{eq:induction} can be written \begin{align*} \mathbb{P}\left[ T_{ 1 : k }^{(N)} \leq t_{ 1 : k }, T_{k+1}^{(N)} > t_{k+1} \right] &= \mathbb{E}\left[ \mathbb{P}[ T_{ 1 : k }^{(N)} \leq t_{ 1 : k }, T_{k+1}^{(N)} > t_{k+1} \mid \mathcal{F}_\infty] \right] \\ &= \mathbb{E} \Bigg[ \sum_{\substack{r_1 <\dots< r_k : \\ r_i \leq \tau_N(t_i) \forall i}} \Big( \prod_{i=1}^k p_{r_i} \Big) \Bigg( \prod_{\substack{r=1 \\ \notin \{r_1,\dots,r_k\} }}^{\tau_N(t)} (1-p_r) \Bigg) \Bigg] . \end{align*} That is, there are jumps at some times $r_{ 1 : k }$, and identity transitions at all other times. A similar expression is derived in \citet{mohle1999}, but here we have an additional expectation because the probabilities $p_r$ depend on the random offspring counts. Lemmata \ref{thm:inductionUB} and \ref{thm:inductionLB} show that this probability converges to the correct limit. This completes the induction.
nodes.statement_short: Induction on the number k of jump times, following Mohle (1999, Lemma 3.2). Base case via Lemma 7, inductive step via upper/lower bounds of Lemmata 8 and 9.

nodes.name: Convergence of joint jump-time distributions
nodes.statement: \lim_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{P}\left[ T_{ 1 : k }^{(N)} \leq t_{ 1 : k } \right] = \mathbb{P}[ T_{ 1 : k } \leq t_{ 1 : k } ] .
nodes.label: eq:518

nodes.name: Induction-step limit
nodes.statement: \lim_{N\to\infty} &\mathbb{P}\left[ T_{ 1 : k }^{(N)} \leq t_{ 1 : k }, T_{k+1}^{(N)} > t_{k+1} \right] = \mathbb{P}[ T_{ 1 : k }\leq t_{ 1 : k }, T_{k+1} > t_{k+1} ].
nodes.label: eq:induction

nodes.name: pass to jump times
nodes.statement: For any $k \in \mathbb{N}$, there is a continuous bijection between the jump times $T_{ 1 : k }^{(N)}$ and the holding times $\varpi_{ 1 : k }^{(N)}$. Thus, convergence of $\varpi_{ 1 : k }^{(N)}$ to $\varpi_{ 1 : k }$ is equivalent to convergence of the jump times to $T_{ 1 : k }$, where $T_i := \varpi_1+\dots+\varpi_i$. We will work with the jump times, following \citet[Lemma 3.2]{mohle1999}.
nodes.statement_short: Equivalently work with jump times

nodes.name: induction statement
nodes.statement: The idea is to prove by induction that, for any $k\in\mathbb{N}$ and $t_{ 1 : k } > 0$, \begin{equation} \lim_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{P}\left[ T_{ 1 : k }^{(N)} \leq t_{ 1 : k } \right] = \mathbb{P}[ T_{ 1 : k } \leq t_{ 1 : k } ] . \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: State the induction hypothesis (9)

nodes.name: base case
nodes.statement: Take the basis case $k=1$, for which $\mathbb{P}[ T_1 \leq t ] = \mathbb{P}[ \varpi_1 \leq t ] = 1 - e^{-\alpha_n t}$ and $T_1^{(N)} >t$ if and only if $( Z_{ \tau_N( t ) } )$ has no jumps up to time $t$: \begin{equation*} \mathbb{P}\left[T_1^{(N)} >t \right] = \mathbb{E}\left[ \mathbb{P}[ T_1^{(N)} >t \mid \mathcal{F}_\infty ] \right] = \mathbb{E}\Bigg[ \prod_{r=1}^{\tau_N(t)} (1-p_r) \Bigg] . \end{equation*} Lemma~\ref{thm:basis} shows that this probability converges to $e^{-\alpha_n t}$ as required.
nodes.statement_short: Base case k=1 via Lemma 7

nodes.name: induction step
nodes.statement: For the induction step, assume that \eqref{eq:518} holds for some $k$. We have \begin{align*} \mathbb{P}\left[ T_{ 1 : ( k + 1 ) }^{(N)} \leq t_{ 1 : ( k + 1 ) } \right] = \mathbb{P}\left[ T_{ 1 : k }^{(N)} \leq t_{ 1 : k } \right] - \mathbb{P}\left[ T_{ 1 : k }^{(N)} \leq t_{ 1 : k }, T_{k+1}^{(N)} > t_{k+1} \right]. \end{align*} The first term on the right-hand side converges to $\mathbb{P}[ T_{ 1 : k } \leq t_{ 1 : k } ]$ by the induction hypothesis, and it remains to show that \begin{align} \lim_{N\to\infty} &\mathbb{P}\left[ T_{ 1 : k }^{(N)} \leq t_{ 1 : k }, T_{k+1}^{(N)} > t_{k+1} \right] = \mathbb{P}[ T_{ 1 : k }\leq t_{ 1 : k }, T_{k+1} > t_{k+1} ]. \end{align}

nodes.name: express both sides

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4
nodes.statement: \textbf{\ref{thm:sumprod1_a}} This follows from the inequalities \begin{equation*} \sum_{\substack{ s_1, \dots, s_l =\tau_N(s) + 1 \\ \text{all distinct} }}^{\tau_N(t)} \prod_{j=1}^l c_N(s_j) \leq \Bigg( \sum_{r=\tau_N(s) + 1}^{\tau_N(t)} c_N(r) \Bigg)^l \leq (t - s + 1)^l, \end{equation*} the first of which follows from a multinomial expansion of the middle term and the second from Proposition~\ref{thm:cN_properties}\ref{item:cN_property4}. \textbf{\ref{thm:sumprod1_b}} We begin by multiplying the bound in \citet[Supplement, equation (8)]{koskela2022erratum} by $\1{\{ c_N(s) \leq t - s\}}$, which is valid because the left-hand side is non-negative, and yields \begin{align*} &\sum_{\substack{ s_1, \dots, s_l =\tau_N(s) + 1 \\ \text{all distinct} }}^{\tau_N(t)} \prod_{j=1}^l c_N(s_j) \\ &\geq \Bigg[ \Bigg( \sum_{r=\tau_N(s) + 1}^{\tau_N(t)} c_N(r) \Bigg)^l \\ &\phantom{\geq \Bigg[} - \Bigg( \sum_{r=\tau_N(s) + 1}^{\tau_N(t)} c_N(r)^2 \Bigg) \binom{l}{2} \Bigg( \sum_{r=\tau_N(s) + 1}^{\tau_N(t)} c_N(r) \Bigg)^{l-2} \Bigg] \1{\{ c_N(\tau_N(s)) \leq t - s\}} \\ &\geq \Bigg[[t - s - c_N(\tau_N(s))]^l - \Bigg( \sum_{r=\tau_N(s) + 1}^{\tau_N(t)} c_N(r)^2 \Bigg) \binom{l}{2} (t + 1)^{l-2}\Bigg]\1{\{c_N(\tau_N(s)) \leq t - s\}}, \end{align*} where the final inequality follows from the definition of $\tau_N$ and Lemma \ref{thm:sumprod1}\ref{thm:sumprod1_a}, and tracking the event $\{c_N(s) \leq t - s\}$ is necessary in case of a large negative value of the lower bound $t - s - c_N(\tau_N(s))$ when $l$ is even. A binomial expansion of the first term on the right-hand side, followed by using Proposition \ref{thm:cN_properties}\ref{item:cN_property1} results in \begin{align*} &\sum_{\substack{ s_1, \dots, s_l =\tau_N(s) + 1 \\ \text{all distinct} }}^{\tau_N(t)} \prod_{j=1}^l c_N(s_j) \\ &\geq \Bigg[(t - s)^l - \sum_{i = 0}^{l - 1} \binom{l}{i} c_N(\tau_N(s))^{l - i} (t - s)^i \\ &\phantom{\geq \Bigg[ (t - s)^l} - \Bigg( \sum_{r=\tau_N(s) + 1}^{\tau_N(t)} c_N(r)^2 \Bigg) \binom{l}{2} (t + 1)^{l-2}\Bigg]\1{\{c_N(\tau_N(s)) \leq t - s\}} \\ &\geq \Bigg[ (t - s)^l - \Bigg( c_N(\tau_N(s)) + \binom{l}{2} \sum_{r = \tau_N(s) + 1}^{\tau_N(t)} c_N(r)^2 \Bigg) (t + 1)^l \Bigg]\1{\{c_N(\tau_N(s)) \leq t - s\}}. \end{align*} For the upper bound we have \begin{align*} \sum_{\substack{ s_1, \dots, s_l =\tau_N(s) + 1 \\ \text{all distinct} }}^{\tau_N(t)} \prod_{j=1}^l c_N(s_j) &\leq \Bigg( \sum_{r=\tau_N(s)+1}^{\tau_N(t)} c_N(s) \Bigg)^l \leq \left[ t - s + c_N(\tau_N(t)) \right]^l , \end{align*} using the definition of $\tau_N$. A binomial expansion and Proposition \ref{thm:cN_properties}\ref{item:cN_property1} yield \begin{align*} [ t - s + c_N(\tau_N(t)) ]^l &= (t - s)^l + \sum_{i=0}^{l-1} \binom{l}{i} (t - s)^i c_N(\tau_N(t))^{l-i}\\ &\leq (t - s)^l + c_N(\tau_N(t)) \sum_{i=0}^{l-1} \binom{l}{i} t^i \\ &\leq (t - s)^l + c_N(\tau_N(t)) (t+1)^l. \end{align*}

otag\ &\leq \sum_{I=0}^{l-1} inom{l}{I} B^{l-I} (t+1)^{l-1} \sum_{s=1}^{	au_N(t)} D_N(s)

nodes.name: Binomial expansion over subsets
nodes.statement: &\sum_{\substack{ s_1, \dots, s_l =1 \\ \text{all distinct} }}^{\tau_N(t)} \prod_{j=1}^l \left[ c_N(s_j) + B D_N(s_j) \right] \notag \\ &= \sum_{\mathcal{I} \subseteq [l]} B^{l-|\mathcal{I}|} \sum_{\substack{ s_1, \dots, s_l =1 \\ \text{all distinct} }}^{\tau_N(t)} \Bigg( \prod_{i\in\mathcal{I}} c_N(s_i) \Bigg) \Bigg( \prod_{j\notin\mathcal{I}} D_N(s_j) \Bigg).

nodes.statement: &\sum_{\mathcal{I} \subseteq [l]} B^{l-|\mathcal{I}|} \sum_{\substack{ s_1, \dots, s_l =1 \\ \text{all distinct} }}^{\tau_N(t)} \Bigg( \prod_{i\in\mathcal{I}} c_N(s_i) \Bigg) \Bigg( \prod_{j\notin\mathcal{I}} D_N(s_j) \Bigg) \notag\\ &= \sum_{\substack{ s_1, \dots, s_l =1 \\ \text{all distinct} }}^{\tau_N(t)} \prod_{j=1}^l c_N(s_j) + \sum_{I=0}^{l-1} \binom{l}{I} B^{l-I} \sum_{\substack{ s_1, \dots, s_l =1 \\ \text{all distinct} }}^{\tau_N(t)} \Bigg( \prod_{i=1}^I c_N(s_i) \Bigg) \Bigg( \prod_{j=I+1}^l D_N(s_j) \Bigg),

\sum_{I=0}^{l-1} inom{l}{I} B^{l-I} &\sum_{\substack{ s_1, \dots, s_l =1 \ 	ext{all distinct} }}^{	au_N(t)} \Bigg( \prod_{i=1}^I c_N(s_i) \Bigg) \Bigg( \prod_{j=I+1}^l D_N(s_j) \Bigg) 
otag\ &\leq \sum_{I=0}^{l-1} inom{l}{I} B^{l-I} \Bigg( \sum_{\substack{ s_1, \dots, s_{l-1} =1 \ 	ext{all distinct} }}^{	au_N(t)} \prod_{i=1}^{l-1} c_N(s_i) \Bigg) \sum_{s_l=1}^{	au_N(t)} D_N(s_l)

nodes.name: binomial expansion
nodes.statement: We start with the binomial expansion \begin{align} &\sum_{\substack{ s_1, \dots, s_l =1 \\ \text{all distinct} }}^{\tau_N(t)} \prod_{j=1}^l \left[ c_N(s_j) + B D_N(s_j) \right] \notag \\ &= \sum_{\mathcal{I} \subseteq [l]} B^{l-|\mathcal{I}|} \sum_{\substack{ s_1, \dots, s_l =1 \\ \text{all distinct} }}^{\tau_N(t)} \Bigg( \prod_{i\in\mathcal{I}} c_N(s_i) \Bigg) \Bigg( \prod_{j\notin\mathcal{I}} D_N(s_j) \Bigg). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Expand the product over subsets

nodes.name: group by size
nodes.statement: Since we are summing over all permutations of $s_{ 1 : l }$, the inner sum depends on $\mathcal{I}$ only through $I:= |\mathcal{I}|$. We may therefore replace the sum over $\mathcal{I} \subseteq [l]$ with a sum over the size $I$ of the subset and a binomial coefficient counting the number of terms in which the subset is of size $I$: \begin{align} &\sum_{\mathcal{I} \subseteq [l]} B^{l-|\mathcal{I}|} \sum_{\substack{ s_1, \dots, s_l =1 \\ \text{all distinct} }}^{\tau_N(t)} \Bigg( \prod_{i\in\mathcal{I}} c_N(s_i) \Bigg) \Bigg( \prod_{j\notin\mathcal{I}} D_N(s_j) \Bigg) \notag\\ &= \sum_{\substack{ s_1, \dots, s_l =1 \\ \text{all distinct} }}^{\tau_N(t)} \prod_{j=1}^l c_N(s_j) + \sum_{I=0}^{l-1} \binom{l}{I} B^{l-I} \sum_{\substack{ s_1, \dots, s_l =1 \\ \text{all distinct} }}^{\tau_N(t)} \Bigg( \prod_{i=1}^I c_N(s_i) \Bigg) \Bigg( \prod_{j=I+1}^l D_N(s_j) \Bigg), \end{align} where we have also separated out the $I = l$ term.
nodes.statement_short: Inner sum depends only on subset size

nodes.name: Sum-product lower bound with D_N perturbation
nodes.statement: Fix $t>0$, $l\in\mathbb{N}$. Then, for any constant $B>0$, \begin{align*} &\sum_{\substack{ s_1, \dots, s_l =1 \\ \text{\normalfont{all distinct}} }}^{\tau_N(t)} \prod_{j=1}^l \left[ c_N(s_j) - B D_N(s_j) \right] \\ &\geq \sum_{\substack{ s_1, \dots, s_l =1 \\ \text{\normalfont{all distinct}} }}^{\tau_N(t)} \prod_{j=1}^l c_N(s_j) - \left( \sum_{s=1}^{\tau_N(t)} D_N(s) \right) (t+1)^{l-1} (1+B)^l . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Subtracting B D_N from each factor lowers the sum-product by at most (sum D_N)(t+1)^{l-1}(1+B)^l.
nodes.label: thm:sumprod3

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 6
nodes.statement: A binomial expansion and manipulations as in \eqref{eq:010}--\eqref{eq:012} gives \begin{align*} &\sum_{\substack{ s_1, \dots, s_l =1 \\ \text{all distinct} }}^{\tau_N(t)} \prod_{j=1}^l \left[ c_N(s_j) - B D_N(s_j) \right] \\ &\geq \sum_{\substack{ s_1, \dots, s_l =1 \\ \text{all distinct} }}^{\tau_N(t)} \prod_{j=1}^l c_N(s_j) - \sum_{I=0}^{l-1} \binom{l}{I} B^{l-I} \sum_{\substack{ s_1, \dots, s_l =1 \\ \text{all distinct} }}^{\tau_N(t)} \Bigg( \prod_{i=1}^I c_N(s_i) \Bigg) \Bigg( \prod_{j=I+1}^l D_N(s_j) \Bigg), \end{align*} where the inequality arises because some positive terms have been multiplied by $-1$. Then \eqref{eq:013} concludes the proof, noting that an upper bound on negative terms results in an overall lower bound.
nodes.statement_short: Same binomial expansion as Lemma 5, then bound (13) on the negative terms.

nodes.name: Ordered-index form of Lemmata 5 and 6
nodes.statement: Since $l$ distinct objects can always be ordered, Lemmata \ref{thm:sumprod2} and \ref{thm:sumprod3} can also be phrased in terms of summations over ordered rather than distinct variables.

nodes.name: Vanishing expectations implied by the merger condition
nodes.statement: The following are all consequences of \eqref{eq:mainthmcondition2}: for all $t>s>0$, \begin{align} \mathbb{E} \left[ c_N(\tau_N(t)) \right] &\rightarrow 0, \\ \mathbb{E}\Bigg[ \sum_{r=\tau_N(s)+1}^{\tau_N(t)} c_N(r)^2 \Bigg] &\rightarrow 0, \\ \mathbb{E}\Bigg[ \sum_{r=\tau_N(s)+1}^{\tau_N(t)} D_N(r) \Bigg] &\rightarrow 0, \end{align} as $N\to\infty$. Proofs are given in \citet{brown2021} in Lemmata 3.4 (with small tweaks), 3.3 and 3.5 respectively.
nodes.statement_short: Condition (5) implies E[c_N(tau_N(t))], E[sum c_N^2] and E[sum D_N] over rescaled intervals all tend to 0.

nodes.name: E[c_N(tau_N(t))] -> 0
nodes.statement: \mathbb{E} \left[ c_N(\tau_N(t)) \right] &\rightarrow 0,

nodes.statement: \mathbb{E}\Bigg[ \sum_{r=\tau_N(s)+1}^{\tau_N(t)} c_N(r)^2 \Bigg] &\rightarrow 0,

nodes.statement: \mathbb{E}\Bigg[ \sum_{r=\tau_N(s)+1}^{\tau_N(t)} D_N(r) \Bigg] &\rightarrow 0,

nodes.name: Basis step
nodes.statement: Assume \eqref{eq:mainthmcondition2} holds. Then for any $0 < t < \infty$, \begin{equation*} \lim_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{E}\Bigg[ \prod_{r=1}^{\tau_N(t)} (1-p_r) \Bigg] = e^{-\alpha_n t}, \end{equation*} where $\alpha_n := n(n-1)/2$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 7
nodes.statement:
We start by showing that $\lim_{N	o\infty}\mathbb{E}[ \prod_{r=1}^{	au_N(t)} (1-p_r) ] \leq e^{-\alpha_n t}$.\ Setting $\xi=\Delta$ in Proposition~ef{thm:pDelta_UB}, we have for each $r$ and sufficiently large $N$,  egin{equation} 1-p_r = p_{\Delta\Delta}(r) \leq 1 - \alpha_n 1_N \left[ c_N(r) - B_n^\prime D_N(r) ight] . \end{equation} Since our interest is the $N	o\infty$ limit, it is sufficient to have bounds that hold for large enough $N$. However, some of the manipulations to follow will also require pre-limiting bounds to be non-negative. For this reason we introduce indicator functions which guarantee non-negativity, but which will not affect the limit. The indicators introduced at this point are such that if their conditions do not hold then the bound becomes the trivial $1-p_r \leq 1$. When $N \geq 3$, a sufficient condition to ensure that the expression on the right-hand side of \eqref{eq:018} is non-negative is that the event  egin{equation} E_N^{1}(r) := \left\{ c_N(r) < \alpha_n^{-1} 1_N ight\} \end{equation} occurs, where the sequence $1_N$ is the same as that in \eqref{eq:018}. We will also need to control the sign of $c_N(r) - B_n^\prime D_N(r)$, for which we define the event  egin{equation} E_N^2(r) := \left\{ c_N(r) \geq B_n^\prime D_N(r) ight\} , \end{equation} and we define $E_N^1 :=  igcap_{r=1}^{	au_N(t)} E_N^1(r)$ and $E_N^2 :=  igcap_{r=1}^{	au_N(t)} E_N^2(r)$. Then  egin{equation*} 1-p_r = p_{\Delta\Delta}(r) \leq 1 - \alpha_n 1_N \left[ c_N(r) - B_n^\prime D_N(r) ight] \1{E_N^1 \cap E_N^2} . \end{equation*} Applying a multinomial expansion and then separating the positive and negative terms,  egin{align} \prod_{r=1}^{	au_N(t)} (1-p_r) &\leq 1 + \sum_{\substack{l=2 \ 	ext{even} }}^{	au_N(t)} \alpha_n^l 1_N  rac{1}{l!} \sum_{\substack{ s_1, \dots, s_l =1 \ 	ext{all distinct} }}^{	au_N(t)} \prod_{j=1}^l \left[ c_N(s_j) - B_n^\prime D_N(s_j) ight] \1{E_N^1 \cap E_N^2} 
otag\ &\phantom{\leq 1} - \sum_{\substack{l=1 \ 	ext{odd} }}^{	au_N(t)} \alpha_n^l 1_N  rac{1}{l!} \sum_{\substack{ s_1, \dots, s_l =1 \ 	ext{all distinct} }}^{	au_N(t)} \prod_{j=1}^l \left[ c_N(s_j) - B_n^\prime D_N(s_j) ight] \1{E_N^1 \cap E_N^2} . \end{align} This is further bounded by applying Lemma~ef{thm:sumprod3} and then both bounds of Lemma~ef{thm:sumprod1}ef{thm:sumprod1_b}:  egin{align*} &\prod_{r=1}^{	au_N(t)} (1-p_r) \ &\leq 1 + \1{E_N^1 \cap E_N^2} \Bigg\{ \sum_{\substack{l=2 \ 	ext{even} }}^{	au_N(t)} \alpha_n^l 1_N  rac{1}{l!} \sum_{\substack{ s_1, \dots, s_l =1 \ 	ext{all distinct} }}^{	au_N(t)} \prod_{j=1}^l c_N(s_j) \ &\phantom{\leq}- \sum_{\substack{l=1 \ 	ext{odd} }}^{	au_N(t)} \alpha_n^l 1_N  rac{1}{l!} \Bigg[ \sum_{\substack{ s_1, \dots, s_l =1 \ 	ext{all distinct} }}^{	au_N(t)} \prod_{j=1}^l c_N(s_j) - \Bigg( \sum_{s=1}^{	au_N(t)} D_N(s) \Bigg) (t+1)^{l-1} (1+B_n^\prime)^l \Bigg] \Bigg\} \ &\leq 1 + \1{E_N^1 \cap E_N^2} \Bigg\{ \sum_{\substack{l=2 \ 	ext{even} }}^{	au_N(t)} \alpha_n^l 1_N  rac{1}{l!} \left\{ t^l + c_N(	au_N(t)) (t+1)^l ight\} \ &\phantom{\leq 1 + \1{E_N^1 \cap E_N^2} \Bigg\{}- \sum_{\substack{l=1 \ 	ext{odd} }}^{	au_N(t)} \alpha_n^l 1_N  rac{1}{l!} \Bigg[ t^l - \Bigg( \sum_{s=1}^{	au_N(t)} c_N(s)^2 \Bigg)  inom{l}{2} (t+1)^l \Bigg] \ &\phantom{\leq 1 + \1{E_N^1 \cap E_N^2} \Bigg\{}- \Bigg( \sum_{s=1}^{	au_N(t)} D_N(s) \Bigg) (t+1)^{l-1} (1+B_n^\prime)^l \Bigg\}. \end{align*} Collecting some terms,  egin{align} &\prod_{r=1}^{	au_N(t)} (1-p_r) \leq 1 + \sum_{l=1}^{	au_N(t)} (-\alpha_n)^l 1_N  rac{1}{l!} t^l \1{E_N^1 \cap E_N^2} + c_N(	au_N(t)) \sum_{\substack{l=2 \ 	ext{even} }}^{	au_N(t)} \alpha_n^l 1_N  rac{1}{l!} (t+1)^l 
otag\ &\phantom{\prod_{r=1}^{	au_N(t)} (1-p_r) \leq 1} + \Bigg( \sum_{s=1}^{	au_N(t)} c_N(s)^2 \Bigg) \sum_{\substack{l=1 \ 	ext{odd} }}^{	au_N(t)} \alpha_n^l 1_N  rac{1}{l!}  inom{l}{2} (t+1)^l 
otag\ &\phantom{\prod_{r=1}^{	au_N(t)} (1-p_r) \leq 1} + \Bigg( \sum_{s=1}^{	au_N(t)} D_N(s) \Bigg) \sum_{\substack{l=1 \ 	ext{odd} }}^{	au_N(t)} \alpha_n^l 1_N  rac{1}{l!} (t+1)^{l-1} (1+B_n^\prime)^l 
otag\ &\phantom{\prod_{r=1}^{	au_N(t)} (1-p_r)}\leq 1 + \sum_{l=1}^{\infty} (-\alpha_n)^l 1_N  rac{1}{l!} t^l \I{	au_N(t) \geq l} \1{E_N^1 \cap E_N^2} + c_N(	au_N(t)) \exp[ \alpha_n 1_N (t+1) ] 
otag\ &\phantom{\prod_{r=1}^{	au_N(t)} (1-p_r) \leq 1} + \Bigg( \sum_{s=1}^{	au_N(t)} c_N(s)^2 \Bigg)  rac{1}{2} \alpha_n^2 (t+1)^2 \exp[ \alpha_n 1_N (t+1) ] 
otag\ &\phantom{\prod_{r=1}^{	au_N(t)} (1-p_r) \leq 1} + \Bigg( \sum_{s=1}^{	au_N(t)} D_N(s) \Bigg) \exp[ \alpha_n 1_N (t+1) (1+B_n^\prime) ] . \end{align} The requirement $	au_N(t) \geq l$ has been dropped in all but the first term, which constitutes adding some positive terms, giving an upper bound. Now, taking the expectation and limit, then applying \eqref{eq:BJJK_eq3.3}--\eqref{eq:BJJK_eq3.4}, and using Lemmata ef{thm:indicators_cN}, ef{thm:indicators_tau} and ef{thm:indicators_DN} to show that $\lim_{N	o\infty} \mathbb{P} \left[ \{	au_N(t) \geq l\} \cap E_N^1 \cap E_N^2 ight] =1$,  egin{align} \lim_{N	o\infty} \mathbb{E} \Bigg[ \prod_{r=1}^{	au_N(t)} (1-p_r) \Bigg] &\leq 1+ \sum_{l=1}^{\infty} (-\alpha_n)^l  rac{1}{l!} t^l \lim_{N	o\infty} \mathbb{P} \left[ \{	au_N(t) \geq l\} \cap E_N^1 \cap E_N^2 ight] 
otag\ &\qquad+ \lim_{N	o\infty} \mathbb{E} \left[ c_N(	au_N(t)) ight] \exp[ \alpha_n (t+1) ] 
otag\ &\qquad+ \lim_{N	o\infty} \mathbb{E} \Bigg[ \sum_{s=1}^{	au_N(t)} c_N(s)^2 \Bigg]  rac{1}{2} \alpha_n^2 (t+1)^2 \exp[ \alpha_n (t+1) ] 
otag\ &\qquad+ \lim_{N	o\infty} \mathbb{E} \Bigg[ \sum_{s=1}^{	au_N(t)} D_N(s) \Bigg] \exp[ \alpha_n (t+1) (1+B_n^\prime) ] 
otag\ &= 1+ \sum_{l=1}^{\infty} (-\alpha_n)^l  rac{1}{l!} t^l = e^{-\alpha_n t}. \end{align} Passing the limit and expectation inside the infinite sum is justified by dominated convergence and Fubini's theorem. It remains to show the corresponding lower bound: $\lim_{N	o\infty} \mathbb{E}[ \prod_{r=1}^{	au_N(t)} (1-p_r) ] \geq e^{-\alpha_n t}$. Setting $\xi=\Delta$ in Proposition~ef{thm:pDelta_LB}, we have  egin{equation} 1-p_t = p_{\Delta\Delta}(t) \geq 1 -  rac{N^{n-2}}{(N-2)_{n-2}} \alpha_n [ c_N(t) + B_n D_N(t) ] , \end{equation} where $B_n >0$. Due to Proposition~ef{thm:cN_properties}ef{item:cN_property1}, a sufficient condition for this bound to be non-negative is  egin{equation} E_N^3(r) := \left\{ c_N(r) \leq  rac{(N-2)_{n-2}}{N^{n-2}} \alpha_n^{-1} (1+B_n)^{-1} ight\} , \end{equation} and we define $E_N^3 :=  igcap_{r=1}^{	au_N(t)} E_N^3(r)$. Then  egin{equation*} 1-p_t \geq \left\{ 1 -  rac{N^{n-2}}{(N-2)_{n-2}} \alpha_n [ c_N(t) + B_n D_N(t) ] ight\} \1{E_N^3(t)} \end{equation*} is also a valid lower bound since if $E_N^3$ does not occur then this collapses to the trivial lower bound $1-p_t \geq 0$. We now apply a multinomial expansion to the product, and split into positive and negative terms:  egin{align} \prod_{r=1}^{	au_N(t)} (1-p_r) &\geq \Bigg\{ 1 + \sum_{\substack{l=2 \ 	ext{even} }}^{	au_N(t)} \alpha_n^l 1_N  rac{1}{l!} \sum_{\substack{ s_1, \dots, s_l =1 \ 	ext{all distinct} }}^{	au_N(t)} \prod_{j=1}^l \left[ c_N(s_j) + B_n D_N(s_j) ight] 
onumber \ &\qquad- \sum_{\substack{l=1 \ 	ext{odd} }}^{	au_N(t)} \alpha_n^l 1_N  rac{1}{l!} \sum_{\substack{ s_1, \dots, s_l =1 \ 	ext{all distinct} }}^{	au_N(t)} \prod_{j=1}^l \left[ c_N(s_j) + B_n D_N(s_j) ight] \Bigg\} \1{E_N^3}. \end{align} From here, the argument for the lower bound follows the same steps as that used to obtain the upper bound. The right-hand side of \eqref{eqlabel_1} is further bounded via Lemma~ef{thm:sumprod2} and both bounds in Lemma~ef{thm:sumprod1}ef{thm:sumprod1_b}:  egin{align*} &\prod_{r=1}^{	au_N(t)} (1-p_r) \ &\geq \1{E_N^3} \Bigg\{ 1 + \sum_{\substack{l=2 \ 	ext{even} }}^{	au_N(t)} \alpha_n^l 1_N  rac{1}{l!} \sum_{\substack{ s_1, \dots, s_l =1 \ 	ext{all distinct} }}^{	au_N(t)} \prod_{j=1}^l c_N(s_j) - \sum_{\substack{l=1 \ 	ext{odd} }}^{	au_N(t)} \alpha_n^l 1_N  rac{1}{l!} \ &\phantom{\geq}	imes \Bigg[ \sum_{\substack{ s_1, \dots, s_l =1 \ 	ext{all distinct} }}^{	au_N(t)} \prod_{j=1}^l c_N(s_j) + \Bigg( \sum_{s=1}^{	au_N(t)} D_N(s) \Bigg) (t+1)^{l-1} (1+B_n)^l \Bigg] \Bigg\} \ &\geq \1{E_N^3} \Bigg\{ 1 + \sum_{\substack{l=2 \ 	ext{even} }}^{	au_N(t)} \alpha_n^l 1_N  rac{1}{l!} \Bigg[ t^l - \Bigg( \sum_{s=1}^{	au_N(t)} c_N(s)^2 \Bigg)  inom{l}{2}(t+1)^l \Bigg] - \sum_{\substack{l=1 \ 	ext{odd} }}^{	au_N(t)} \alpha_n^l \ &\phantom{\geq} 	imes 1_N  rac{1}{l!} \Bigg[ t^l + c_N(	au_N(t)) (t+1)^l + \Bigg( \sum_{s=1}^{	au_N(t)} D_N(s) \Bigg) (t+1)^{l-1} (1+B_n)^l \Bigg] \Bigg\} . \end{align*} Collecting terms and dropping indicators from some non-positive terms,  egin{align} \prod_{r=1}^{	au_N(t)} (1-p_r) &\geq \sum_{l=0}^{	au_N(t)} (-\alpha_n)^l 1_N  rac{1}{l!} t^l \1{E_N^3} - c_N(	au_N(t)) \sum_{\substack{l=1 \ 	ext{odd} }}^{	au_N(t)} \alpha_n^l 1_N  rac{1}{l!} (t+1)^l

otag\ &\phantom{\leq 1} - \sum_{\substack{l=1 \ 	ext{odd} }}^{	au_N(t)} \alpha_n^l 1_N  rac{1}{l!} \sum_{\substack{ s_1, \dots, s_l =1 \ 	ext{all distinct} }}^{	au_N(t)} \prod_{j=1}^l \left[ c_N(s_j) - B_n^\prime D_N(s_j) ight] \1{E_N^1 \cap E_N^2} . \end{align} This is further bounded by applying Lemma~ef{thm:sumprod3} and then both bounds of Lemma~ef{thm:sumprod1}ef{thm:sumprod1_b}:  egin{align*} &\prod_{r=1}^{	au_N(t)} (1-p_r) \ &\leq 1 + \1{E_N^1 \cap E_N^2} \Bigg\{ \sum_{\substack{l=2 \ 	ext{even} }}^{	au_N(t)} \alpha_n^l 1_N  rac{1}{l!} \sum_{\substack{ s_1, \dots, s_l =1 \ 	ext{all distinct} }}^{	au_N(t)} \prod_{j=1}^l c_N(s_j) \ &\phantom{\leq}- \sum_{\substack{l=1 \ 	ext{odd} }}^{	au_N(t)} \alpha_n^l 1_N  rac{1}{l!} \Bigg[ \sum_{\substack{ s_1, \dots, s_l =1 \ 	ext{all distinct} }}^{	au_N(t)} \prod_{j=1}^l c_N(s_j) - \Bigg( \sum_{s=1}^{	au_N(t)} D_N(s) \Bigg) (t+1)^{l-1} (1+B_n^\prime)^l \Bigg] \Bigg\} \ &\leq 1 + \1{E_N^1 \cap E_N^2} \Bigg\{ \sum_{\substack{l=2 \ 	ext{even} }}^{	au_N(t)} \alpha_n^l 1_N  rac{1}{l!} \left\{ t^l + c_N(	au_N(t)) (t+1)^l ight\} \ &\phantom{\leq 1 + \1{E_N^1 \cap E_N^2} \Bigg\{}- \sum_{\substack{l=1 \ 	ext{odd} }}^{	au_N(t)} \alpha_n^l 1_N  rac{1}{l!} \Bigg[ t^l - \Bigg( \sum_{s=1}^{	au_N(t)} c_N(s)^2 \Bigg)  inom{l}{2} (t+1)^l \Bigg] \ &\phantom{\leq 1 + \1{E_N^1 \cap E_N^2} \Bigg\{}- \Bigg( \sum_{s=1}^{	au_N(t)} D_N(s) \Bigg) (t+1)^{l-1} (1+B_n^\prime)^l \Bigg\}. \end{align*} Collecting some terms,  egin{align} &\prod_{r=1}^{	au_N(t)} (1-p_r) \leq 1 + \sum_{l=1}^{	au_N(t)} (-\alpha_n)^l 1_N  rac{1}{l!} t^l \1{E_N^1 \cap E_N^2} + c_N(	au_N(t)) \sum_{\substack{l=2 \ 	ext{even} }}^{	au_N(t)} \alpha_n^l 1_N  rac{1}{l!} (t+1)^l

otag\ &\qquad+ \lim_{N	o\infty} \mathbb{E} \left[ c_N(	au_N(t)) ight] \exp[ \alpha_n (t+1) ]

otag\ &= 1+ \sum_{l=1}^{\infty} (-\alpha_n)^l  rac{1}{l!} t^l = e^{-\alpha_n t}. \end{align} Passing the limit and expectation inside the infinite sum is justified by dominated convergence and Fubini's theorem.

nodes.statement: This is further bounded by applying Lemma~\ref{thm:sumprod3} and then both bounds of Lemma~\ref{thm:sumprod1}\ref{thm:sumprod1_b}: \begin{align*} &\prod_{r=1}^{\tau_N(t)} (1-p_r) \\ &\leq 1 + \1{E_N^1 \cap E_N^2} \Bigg\{ \sum_{\substack{l=2 \\ \text{even} }}^{\tau_N(t)} \alpha_n^l 1_N \frac{1}{l!} \sum_{\substack{ s_1, \dots, s_l =1 \\ \text{all distinct} }}^{\tau_N(t)} \prod_{j=1}^l c_N(s_j) \\ &\phantom{\leq}- \sum_{\substack{l=1 \\ \text{odd} }}^{\tau_N(t)} \alpha_n^l 1_N \frac{1}{l!} \Bigg[ \sum_{\substack{ s_1, \dots, s_l =1 \\ \text{all distinct} }}^{\tau_N(t)} \prod_{j=1}^l c_N(s_j) - \Bigg( \sum_{s=1}^{\tau_N(t)} D_N(s) \Bigg) (t+1)^{l-1} (1+B_n^\prime)^l \Bigg] \Bigg\} \\ &\leq 1 + \1{E_N^1 \cap E_N^2} \Bigg\{ \sum_{\substack{l=2 \\ \text{even} }}^{\tau_N(t)} \alpha_n^l 1_N \frac{1}{l!} \left\{ t^l + c_N(\tau_N(t)) (t+1)^l \right\} \\ &\phantom{\leq 1 + \1{E_N^1 \cap E_N^2} \Bigg\{}- \sum_{\substack{l=1 \\ \text{odd} }}^{\tau_N(t)} \alpha_n^l 1_N \frac{1}{l!} \Bigg[ t^l - \Bigg( \sum_{s=1}^{\tau_N(t)} c_N(s)^2 \Bigg) \binom{l}{2} (t+1)^l \Bigg] \\ &\phantom{\leq 1 + \1{E_N^1 \cap E_N^2} \Bigg\{}- \Bigg( \sum_{s=1}^{\tau_N(t)} D_N(s) \Bigg) (t+1)^{l-1} (1+B_n^\prime)^l \Bigg\}. \end{align*}

nodes.name: collect terms
nodes.statement:
Collecting some terms,  egin{align} &\prod_{r=1}^{	au_N(t)} (1-p_r) \leq 1 + \sum_{l=1}^{	au_N(t)} (-\alpha_n)^l 1_N  rac{1}{l!} t^l \1{E_N^1 \cap E_N^2} + c_N(	au_N(t)) \sum_{\substack{l=2 \ 	ext{even} }}^{	au_N(t)} \alpha_n^l 1_N  rac{1}{l!} (t+1)^l 
otag\ &\phantom{\prod_{r=1}^{	au_N(t)} (1-p_r) \leq 1} + \Bigg( \sum_{s=1}^{	au_N(t)} c_N(s)^2 \Bigg) \sum_{\substack{l=1 \ 	ext{odd} }}^{	au_N(t)} \alpha_n^l 1_N  rac{1}{l!}  inom{l}{2} (t+1)^l 
otag\ &\phantom{\prod_{r=1}^{	au_N(t)} (1-p_r) \leq 1} + \Bigg( \sum_{s=1}^{	au_N(t)} D_N(s) \Bigg) \sum_{\substack{l=1 \ 	ext{odd} }}^{	au_N(t)} \alpha_n^l 1_N  rac{1}{l!} (t+1)^{l-1} (1+B_n^\prime)^l 
otag\ &\phantom{\prod_{r=1}^{	au_N(t)} (1-p_r)}\leq 1 + \sum_{l=1}^{\infty} (-\alpha_n)^l 1_N  rac{1}{l!} t^l \I{	au_N(t) \geq l} \1{E_N^1 \cap E_N^2} + c_N(	au_N(t)) \exp[ \alpha_n 1_N (t+1) ] 
otag\ &\phantom{\prod_{r=1}^{	au_N(t)} (1-p_r) \leq 1} + \Bigg( \sum_{s=1}^{	au_N(t)} c_N(s)^2 \Bigg)  rac{1}{2} \alpha_n^2 (t+1)^2 \exp[ \alpha_n 1_N (t+1) ] 
otag\ &\phantom{\prod_{r=1}^{	au_N(t)} (1-p_r) \leq 1} + \Bigg( \sum_{s=1}^{	au_N(t)} D_N(s) \Bigg) \exp[ \alpha_n 1_N (t+1) (1+B_n^\prime) ] . \end{align} The requirement $	au_N(t) \geq l$ has been dropped in all but the first term, which constitutes adding some positive terms, giving an upper bound.
nodes.statement_short: Collect into exponential series plus error terms

nodes.name: take limit
nodes.statement:
Now, taking the expectation and limit, then applying \eqref{eq:BJJK_eq3.3}--\eqref{eq:BJJK_eq3.4}, and using Lemmata ef{thm:indicators_cN}, ef{thm:indicators_tau} and ef{thm:indicators_DN} to show that $\lim_{N	o\infty} \mathbb{P} \left[ \{	au_N(t) \geq l\} \cap E_N^1 \cap E_N^2 ight] =1$,  egin{align} \lim_{N	o\infty} \mathbb{E} \Bigg[ \prod_{r=1}^{	au_N(t)} (1-p_r) \Bigg] &\leq 1+ \sum_{l=1}^{\infty} (-\alpha_n)^l  rac{1}{l!} t^l \lim_{N	o\infty} \mathbb{P} \left[ \{	au_N(t) \geq l\} \cap E_N^1 \cap E_N^2 ight] 
otag\ &\qquad+ \lim_{N	o\infty} \mathbb{E} \left[ c_N(	au_N(t)) ight] \exp[ \alpha_n (t+1) ] 
otag\ &\qquad+ \lim_{N	o\infty} \mathbb{E} \Bigg[ \sum_{s=1}^{	au_N(t)} c_N(s)^2 \Bigg]  rac{1}{2} \alpha_n^2 (t+1)^2 \exp[ \alpha_n (t+1) ] 
otag\ &\qquad+ \lim_{N	o\infty} \mathbb{E} \Bigg[ \sum_{s=1}^{	au_N(t)} D_N(s) \Bigg] \exp[ \alpha_n (t+1) (1+B_n^\prime) ] 
otag\ &= 1+ \sum_{l=1}^{\infty} (-\alpha_n)^l  rac{1}{l!} t^l = e^{-\alpha_n t}. \end{align} Passing the limit and expectation inside the infinite sum is justified by dominated convergence and Fubini's theorem.
nodes.statement_short: Error terms vanish; indicators tend to 1

nodes.name: lower bound
nodes.statement:
It remains to show the corresponding lower bound: $\lim_{N	o\infty} \mathbb{E}[ \prod_{r=1}^{	au_N(t)} (1-p_r) ] \geq e^{-\alpha_n t}$. Setting $\xi=\Delta$ in Proposition~ef{thm:pDelta_LB}, we have  egin{equation} 1-p_t = p_{\Delta\Delta}(t) \geq 1 -  rac{N^{n-2}}{(N-2)_{n-2}} \alpha_n [ c_N(t) + B_n D_N(t) ] , \end{equation} where $B_n >0$. Due to Proposition~ef{thm:cN_properties}ef{item:cN_property1}, a sufficient condition for this bound to be non-negative is  egin{equation} E_N^3(r) := \left\{ c_N(r) \leq  rac{(N-2)_{n-2}}{N^{n-2}} \alpha_n^{-1} (1+B_n)^{-1} ight\} , \end{equation} and we define $E_N^3 :=  igcap_{r=1}^{	au_N(t)} E_N^3(r)$. Then  egin{equation*} 1-p_t \geq \left\{ 1 -  rac{N^{n-2}}{(N-2)_{n-2}} \alpha_n [ c_N(t) + B_n D_N(t) ] ight\} \1{E_N^3(t)} \end{equation*} is also a valid lower bound since if $E_N^3$ does not occur then this collapses to the trivial lower bound $1-p_t \geq 0$. We now apply a multinomial expansion to the product, and split into positive and negative terms:  egin{align} \prod_{r=1}^{	au_N(t)} (1-p_r) &\geq \Bigg\{ 1 + \sum_{\substack{l=2 \ 	ext{even} }}^{	au_N(t)} \alpha_n^l 1_N  rac{1}{l!} \sum_{\substack{ s_1, \dots, s_l =1 \ 	ext{all distinct} }}^{	au_N(t)} \prod_{j=1}^l \left[ c_N(s_j) + B_n D_N(s_j) ight] 
onumber \ &\qquad- \sum_{\substack{l=1 \ 	ext{odd} }}^{	au_N(t)} \alpha_n^l 1_N  rac{1}{l!} \sum_{\substack{ s_1, \dots, s_l =1 \ 	ext{all distinct} }}^{	au_N(t)} \prod_{j=1}^l \left[ c_N(s_j) + B_n D_N(s_j) ight] \Bigg\} \1{E_N^3}. \end{align} From here, the argument for the lower bound follows the same steps as that used to obtain the upper bound. The right-hand side of \eqref{eqlabel_1} is further bounded via Lemma~ef{thm:sumprod2} and both bounds in Lemma~ef{thm:sumprod1}ef{thm:sumprod1_b}:  egin{align*} &\prod_{r=1}^{	au_N(t)} (1-p_r) \ &\geq \1{E_N^3} \Bigg\{ 1 + \sum_{\substack{l=2 \ 	ext{even} }}^{	au_N(t)} \alpha_n^l 1_N  rac{1}{l!} \sum_{\substack{ s_1, \dots, s_l =1 \ 	ext{all distinct} }}^{	au_N(t)} \prod_{j=1}^l c_N(s_j) - \sum_{\substack{l=1 \ 	ext{odd} }}^{	au_N(t)} \alpha_n^l 1_N  rac{1}{l!} \ &\phantom{\geq}	imes \Bigg[ \sum_{\substack{ s_1, \dots, s_l =1 \ 	ext{all distinct} }}^{	au_N(t)} \prod_{j=1}^l c_N(s_j) + \Bigg( \sum_{s=1}^{	au_N(t)} D_N(s) \Bigg) (t+1)^{l-1} (1+B_n)^l \Bigg] \Bigg\} \ &\geq \1{E_N^3} \Bigg\{ 1 + \sum_{\substack{l=2 \ 	ext{even} }}^{	au_N(t)} \alpha_n^l 1_N  rac{1}{l!} \Bigg[ t^l - \Bigg( \sum_{s=1}^{	au_N(t)} c_N(s)^2 \Bigg)  inom{l}{2}(t+1)^l \Bigg] - \sum_{\substack{l=1 \ 	ext{odd} }}^{	au_N(t)} \alpha_n^l \ &\phantom{\geq} 	imes 1_N  rac{1}{l!} \Bigg[ t^l + c_N(	au_N(t)) (t+1)^l + \Bigg( \sum_{s=1}^{	au_N(t)} D_N(s) \Bigg) (t+1)^{l-1} (1+B_n)^l \Bigg] \Bigg\} . \end{align*} Collecting terms and dropping indicators from some non-positive terms,  egin{align} \prod_{r=1}^{	au_N(t)} (1-p_r) &\geq \sum_{l=0}^{	au_N(t)} (-\alpha_n)^l 1_N  rac{1}{l!} t^l \1{E_N^3} - c_N(	au_N(t)) \sum_{\substack{l=1 \ 	ext{odd} }}^{	au_N(t)} \alpha_n^l 1_N  rac{1}{l!} (t+1)^l 
otag\ &\qquad- \Bigg( \sum_{s=1}^{	au_N(t)} c_N(s)^2 \Bigg) \sum_{\substack{l=2 \ 	ext{even} }}^{	au_N(t)} \alpha_n^l 1_N  rac{1}{l!}  inom{l}{2}(t+1)^l 
otag\ &\qquad- \Bigg( \sum_{s=1}^{	au_N(t)} D_N(s) \Bigg) \sum_{\substack{l=1 \ 	ext{odd} }}^{	au_N(t)} \alpha_n^l 1_N  rac{1}{l!} (t+1)^{l-1} (1+B_n)^l 
otag\ &\geq \sum_{l=0}^{\infty} (-\alpha_n)^l 1_N  rac{1}{l!} t^l \1{E_N^3} \I{ 	au_N(t) \geq l} - c_N(	au_N(t)) \exp[ \alpha_n 1_N (t+1) ] 
otag \ &\qquad - \Bigg( \sum_{s=1}^{	au_N(t)} c_N(s)^2 \Bigg)  rac{1}{2} \alpha_n^2 (t+1)^2 \exp[ \alpha_n 1_N (t+1) ]
otag\ &\qquad- \Bigg( \sum_{s=1}^{	au_N(t)} D_N(s) \Bigg) \exp[ \alpha_n 1_N (t+1) (1+B_n) ]. \end{align} Now, taking the expectation and limit, and applying \eqref{eq:BJJK_eq3.3}--\eqref{eq:BJJK_eq3.4} to show that all but the first sum vanish, and Lemmata ef{thm:indicators_cN} and ef{thm:indicators_tau} to show that $\lim_{N	o\infty} \mathbb{P}[ \{	au_N(t) \geq l\} \cap E_N^3 ] =1$,  egin{align} \lim_{N	o\infty} \mathbb{E} \Bigg[ \prod_{r=1}^{	au_N(t)} (1-p_r) \Bigg] &\geq \sum_{l=0}^{\infty} (-\alpha_n)^l 1_N  rac{1}{l!} t^l \lim_{N	o\infty} \mathbb{P}\left[ \{	au_N(t) \geq l\} \cap E_N^3 ight] 
otag\ &\qquad- \lim_{N	o\infty} \mathbb{E} \Bigg[ \sum_{s=1}^{	au_N(t)} c_N(s)^2 \Bigg]  rac{1}{2} \alpha_n^2 (t+1)^2 \exp[ \alpha_n (t+1) ]
otag\ &\qquad- \lim_{N	o\infty} \mathbb{E} \Bigg[ c_N(	au_N(t)) \Bigg] \exp[ \alpha_n (t+1) ] 
otag\ &\qquad- \lim_{N	o\infty} \mathbb{E} \Bigg[ \sum_{s=1}^{	au_N(t)} D_N(s) \Bigg] \exp[ \alpha_n (t+1) (1+B_n) ] 
otag\ &= \sum_{l=0}^{\infty} (-\alpha_n)^l  rac{1}{l!} t^l = e^{-\alpha_n t}. \end{align} Again, passing the limit and expectation inside the infinite sum is justified by dominated convergence and Fubini.
nodes.statement_short: Prove the limit is at least exp(-alpha_n t)

nodes.name: goal

nodes.statement: Then \begin{equation*} 1-p_t \geq \left\{ 1 - \frac{N^{n-2}}{(N-2)_{n-2}} \alpha_n [ c_N(t) + B_n D_N(t) ] \right\} \1{E_N^3(t)} \end{equation*} is also a valid lower bound since if $E_N^3$ does not occur then this collapses to the trivial lower bound $1-p_t \geq 0$.

nodes.name: expand product
nodes.statement: We now apply a multinomial expansion to the product, and split into positive and negative terms: \begin{align} \prod_{r=1}^{\tau_N(t)} (1-p_r) &\geq \Bigg\{ 1 + \sum_{\substack{l=2 \\ \text{even} }}^{\tau_N(t)} \alpha_n^l 1_N \frac{1}{l!} \sum_{\substack{ s_1, \dots, s_l =1 \\ \text{all distinct} }}^{\tau_N(t)} \prod_{j=1}^l \left[ c_N(s_j) + B_n D_N(s_j) \right] \nonumber \\ &\qquad- \sum_{\substack{l=1 \\ \text{odd} }}^{\tau_N(t)} \alpha_n^l 1_N \frac{1}{l!} \sum_{\substack{ s_1, \dots, s_l =1 \\ \text{all distinct} }}^{\tau_N(t)} \prod_{j=1}^l \left[ c_N(s_j) + B_n D_N(s_j) \right] \Bigg\} \1{E_N^3}. \end{align} From here, the argument for the lower bound follows the same steps as that used to obtain the upper bound.

nodes.statement:
Collecting terms and dropping indicators from some non-positive terms,  egin{align} \prod_{r=1}^{	au_N(t)} (1-p_r) &\geq \sum_{l=0}^{	au_N(t)} (-\alpha_n)^l 1_N  rac{1}{l!} t^l \1{E_N^3} - c_N(	au_N(t)) \sum_{\substack{l=1 \ 	ext{odd} }}^{	au_N(t)} \alpha_n^l 1_N  rac{1}{l!} (t+1)^l 
otag\ &\qquad- \Bigg( \sum_{s=1}^{	au_N(t)} c_N(s)^2 \Bigg) \sum_{\substack{l=2 \ 	ext{even} }}^{	au_N(t)} \alpha_n^l 1_N  rac{1}{l!}  inom{l}{2}(t+1)^l 
otag\ &\qquad- \Bigg( \sum_{s=1}^{	au_N(t)} D_N(s) \Bigg) \sum_{\substack{l=1 \ 	ext{odd} }}^{	au_N(t)} \alpha_n^l 1_N  rac{1}{l!} (t+1)^{l-1} (1+B_n)^l 
otag\ &\geq \sum_{l=0}^{\infty} (-\alpha_n)^l 1_N  rac{1}{l!} t^l \1{E_N^3} \I{ 	au_N(t) \geq l} - c_N(	au_N(t)) \exp[ \alpha_n 1_N (t+1) ] 
otag \ &\qquad - \Bigg( \sum_{s=1}^{	au_N(t)} c_N(s)^2 \Bigg)  rac{1}{2} \alpha_n^2 (t+1)^2 \exp[ \alpha_n 1_N (t+1) ]
otag\ &\qquad- \Bigg( \sum_{s=1}^{	au_N(t)} D_N(s) \Bigg) \exp[ \alpha_n 1_N (t+1) (1+B_n) ]. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Collect into series plus error terms

nodes.name: take limit
nodes.statement:
Now, taking the expectation and limit, and applying \eqref{eq:BJJK_eq3.3}--\eqref{eq:BJJK_eq3.4} to show that all but the first sum vanish, and Lemmata ef{thm:indicators_cN} and ef{thm:indicators_tau} to show that $\lim_{N	o\infty} \mathbb{P}[ \{	au_N(t) \geq l\} \cap E_N^3 ] =1$,  egin{align} \lim_{N	o\infty} \mathbb{E} \Bigg[ \prod_{r=1}^{	au_N(t)} (1-p_r) \Bigg] &\geq \sum_{l=0}^{\infty} (-\alpha_n)^l 1_N  rac{1}{l!} t^l \lim_{N	o\infty} \mathbb{P}\left[ \{	au_N(t) \geq l\} \cap E_N^3 ight] 
otag\ &\qquad- \lim_{N	o\infty} \mathbb{E} \Bigg[ \sum_{s=1}^{	au_N(t)} c_N(s)^2 \Bigg]  rac{1}{2} \alpha_n^2 (t+1)^2 \exp[ \alpha_n (t+1) ]
otag\ &\qquad- \lim_{N	o\infty} \mathbb{E} \Bigg[ c_N(	au_N(t)) \Bigg] \exp[ \alpha_n (t+1) ]

otag\ &= \sum_{l=0}^{\infty} (-\alpha_n)^l  rac{1}{l!} t^l = e^{-\alpha_n t}. \end{align} Again, passing the limit and expectation inside the infinite sum is justified by dominated convergence and Fubini.

nodes.name: combine
nodes.statement: Combining the upper and lower bounds in \eqref{eq:022} and \eqref{eq:029} respectively concludes the proof.

nodes.name: Induction step upper bound
nodes.statement: Assume \eqref{eq:mainthmcondition2} holds. Fix $k \in \mathbb{N}$, $i_0:=0$, $i_k:=k$. For any sequence of times $0 = t_0 \leq t_1 \leq \cdots \leq t_k \leq t$, \begin{align*} \lim_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{E} \Bigg[ \sum_{\substack{r_1 <\dots< r_k :\\ r_i \leq \tau_N(t_i) \forall i}} &\Bigg( \prod_{i=1}^k p_{r_i} \Bigg) \Bigg( \prod_{\substack{r=1 \\ \notin \{r_1,\dots,r_k\} }}^{\tau_N(t)} (1-p_r) \Bigg) \Bigg] \\ &\leq \alpha_n^k e^{-\alpha_n t} \sum_{\substack{i_1\leq \dots\leq i_{k-1}\\ \in \{0,\dots,k\} : i_j \geq j}} \prod_{j=1}^k \frac{(t_j - t_{j-1})^{i_j - i_{j-1}}}{(i_j - i_{j-1})! } . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Upper bound on the limiting probability of k jumps by given times followed by no further jump, matching the Kingman value.

The upper and lower bounds coincide, so the proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Decompose by intervals (Mohle), bound each block with Lemma 4(b) from above and below, and pass to the limit with (14)-(15).

nodes.name: decompose
nodes.statement: As pointed out by \citet[p.\ 460]{mohle1999}, the sum-product on the left-hand side of the statement can be expanded as \begin{equation*} \sum_{\substack{r_1<\dots<r_k :\\ r_i\leq \tau_N(t_i) \forall i}} \prod_{i=1}^k c_N(r_i) = \sum_{\substack{i_1\leq \dots\leq i_{k-1}\\ \in \{0,\dots,k\} : i_j \geq j}} \, \prod_{j=1}^k \frac{1}{(i_j - i_{j-1})!} \sum_{\substack{ r_{i_{j-1}+1}, \ldots, r_{i_j} \\ = \tau_N(t_{j-1})+1 \\ \text{all distinct} }}^{\tau_N(t_j)} \,\prod_{i=i_{j-1}+1}^{i_j} c_N(r_i) . \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Expand sum-product by intervals (Mohle)

nodes.name: upper bound blocks
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{thm:sumprod1}\ref{thm:sumprod1_b}, \begin{align*} \sum_{\substack{ r_{i_{j-1}+1}, \ldots, r_{i_j} = \tau_N(t_{j-1})+1 \\ \text{all distinct} }}^{\tau_N(t_j)} \prod_{i=i_{j-1}+1}^{i_j} c_N(r_i) \leq{}& (t_j - t_{j-1})^{i_j - i_{j-1}} \\& + c_N(\tau_N(t_j)) ( t_j +1 )^{i_j - i_{j-1}}. \end{align*} Hence, a $k$-fold product of similar terms can be bounded as \begin{align*} &\prod_{j=1}^k \frac{1}{(i_j - i_{j-1})!} \sum_{\substack{ r_{i_{j-1}+1}, \ldots, r_{i_j} = \tau_N(t_{j-1})+1 \\ \text{all distinct} }}^{\tau_N(t_j)} \,\prod_{i=i_{j-1}+1}^{i_j} c_N(r_i) \\ &\leq \prod_{j=1}^k \Bigg\{ \frac{(t_j - t_{j-1})^{i_j - i_{j-1}}}{(i_j - i_{j-1})!} + c_N(\tau_N(t_j)) \frac{( t_j +1 )^{i_j - i_{j-1}}}{(i_j - i_{j-1})!} \Bigg\} \\ &\leq \prod_{j=1}^k \frac{(t_j - t_{j-1})^{i_j - i_{j-1}}}{(i_j - i_{j-1})!} + \sum_{\mathcal{I} \subset [k]} \left( \prod_{j\in\mathcal{I}} t^{i_j - i_{j-1}}\right) \Bigg( \prod_{j\notin\mathcal{I}} c_N(\tau_N(t_j)) (t+1)^{i_j - i_{j-1}} \Bigg) \\ &\leq \prod_{j=1}^k \frac{(t_j - t_{j-1})^{i_j - i_{j-1}}}{(i_j - i_{j-1})!} + \sum_{\mathcal{I} \subset [k]} c_N(\tau_N(t_{j^\star(\mathcal{I})})) ( t+1 )^k, \end{align*} where, say, $j^\star(\mathcal{I}) := \min\{ j\notin\mathcal{I}\}$, and the second-to-last line follows by separating the $I = [k]$ term, and the last via Proposition \ref{thm:cN_properties}\ref{item:cN_property1}, recalling that $t_0 = 0$ and $t = t_k$.
nodes.statement_short: Upper bound each block with Lemma 4(b)

nodes.name: upper limit
nodes.statement: Now we are in a position to evaluate the desired limit: \begin{align*} &\lim_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{E} \Bigg[ \1{E_N} \sum_{\substack{r_1<\dots<r_k :\\ r_i\leq \tau_N(t_i) \forall i}} \prod_{i=1}^k c_N(r_i) \Bigg] \leq \lim_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{E} \Bigg[\sum_{\substack{r_1<\dots<r_k :\\ r_i\leq \tau_N(t_i) \forall i}} \prod_{i=1}^k c_N(r_i) \Bigg] \\ &\leq \sum_{\substack{i_1\leq \dots\leq i_{k-1}\\ \in \{0,\dots,k\} : i_j \geq j}} \Bigg\{ \prod_{j=1}^k \frac{(t_j - t_{j-1})^{i_j - i_{j-1}}} {(i_j - i_{j-1})!} + \sum_{\mathcal{I} \subset [k]} \lim_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{E} [ c_N(\tau_N(t_{j^\star(\mathcal{I})})) ] (t+1)^k \Bigg\} \\ &= \sum_{\substack{i_1\leq \dots\leq i_{k-1}\\ \in \{0,\dots,k\} : i_j \geq j \forall j}} \prod_{j=1}^k \frac{(t_j - t_{j-1})^{i_j - i_{j-1}}} {(i_j - i_{j-1})!}, \end{align*} using \eqref{eq:BJJK_eq3.3}.
nodes.statement_short: Upper limit via (14)

nodes.name: lower bound blocks
nodes.statement: For the corresponding lower bound, by Lemma~\ref{thm:sumprod1}\ref{thm:sumprod1_b}, \begin{align*} &\sum_{\substack{ r_{i_{j-1}+1}, \ldots, r_{i_j} = \tau_N(t_{j-1})+1 \\ \text{all distinct} }}^{\tau_N(t_j)} \prod_{i=i_{j-1}+1}^{i_j} c_N(r_i) \\ &\geq \Bigg[(t_j - t_{j-1})^{i_j - i_{j-1}} - \Bigg(c_N(\tau_N(t_{j - 1})) \\ &\phantom{\geq \Bigg[} + \binom{i_j - i_{j-1}}{2} \sum_{s=\tau_N(t_{j-1})+1}^{\tau_N(t_j)} c_N(s)^2 \Bigg) ( t_j + 1 )^{i_j - i_{j-1}} \Bigg] \1{\{c_N(\tau_N(t_{j - 1})) \leq t_j - t_{j - 1}\}}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Lower bound each block with Lemma 4(b)

nodes.name: good events

Define the events  egin{align*} E_N^4(j) &= \Bigg\{ \sum_{s=	au_N(t_{j-1})+1}^{	au_N(t_j)} c_N(s)^2 \leq  rac{1}{2(i_j - i_{j - 1})!} \Bigg(  rac{ t_j - t_{j-1} }{ t_j +1 }\Bigg)^{i_j - i_{j-1}} \Bigg\}, \ F_N^4(j) &= \Bigg\{ c_N(	au_N(t_{j-1})) \leq  rac{1}{2(i_j - i_{j - 1})!} \Bigg(  rac{ t_j - t_{j-1} }{ t_j +1 }\Bigg)^{i_j - i_{j-1}} \Bigg\}, \end{align*} where the upper bound on the right-hand sides is strictly positive since $t_j > t_{j - 1}$, and thus satisfies the conditions of Lemmata ef{thm:indicators_cN} and ef{thm:indicators_c2}. otin\mathcal{I}} \Bigg( c_N(	au_N(t_{j - 1} )) + \sum_{s=	au_N(t_{j-1})+1} ^{	au_N(t_j)} c_N(s)^2 \Bigg) ( t+1 )^{i_j - i_{j-1}} \Bigg), \end{align*} where the last expression separates out the $\mathcal{I} = [k]$ term, ensures all other terms have a negative sign, and bounds their magnitude from above.
nodes.statement_short: Define events making factors non-negative and expand

nodes.name: simplify
nodes.statement: Using parts \ref{item:cN_property1} and \ref{item:cN_property4} of Proposition~\ref{thm:cN_properties} to upper bound all but one of the $c_N(\tau_N(t_{j-1})) + \sum c_N(s)^2 \leq t + 2$ factors, arbitrarily setting $j^\star(\mathcal{I}) := \min\{j \notin \mathcal{I} \}$, as well as recalling that $\sum_{ j = 1 }^k (i_j - i_{j - 1}) = k$ and $|\mathcal{I}^c| \leq k$, this is further bounded by \begin{align*} &\prod_{j=1}^k \frac{1}{(i_j - i_{j-1})!} \sum_{\substack{ r_{i_{j-1}+1}, \ldots, r_{i_j} = \tau_N(t_{j-1})+1 \\ \text{all distinct} }}^{\tau_N(t_j)} \,\prod_{i=i_{j-1}+1}^{i_j} c_N(r_i) \notag\\ &\geq \prod_{j=1}^k \frac{(t_j - t_{j-1})^{i_j - i_{j-1}}}{(i_j - i_{j-1})!} \1{E_N^4} - \sum_{\mathcal{I} \subset [k]} \Bigg( c_N(\tau_N(t_{j^*(I)-1})) + \sum_{s=\tau_N(t_{j^\star(\mathcal{I})-1})+1} ^{\tau_N(t_{j^\star(\mathcal{I})})} c_N(s)^2 \Bigg) ( t+2 )^{2 k} . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Bound all but one factor

nodes.name: lower limit and conclude
nodes.statement: We can now evaluate the limit: \begin{align*} &\lim_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{E} \Bigg[ \1{E_N} \sum_{\substack{r_1<\dots<r_k :\\ r_i\leq \tau_N(t_i) \forall i}} \prod_{i=1}^k c_N(r_i) \Bigg] \\ &\geq \sum_{\substack{i_1\leq \dots\leq i_{k-1}\\ \in \{0,\dots,k\} : i_j \geq j}} \prod_{j=1}^k \frac{(t_j - t_{j-1})^{i_j - i_{j-1}}}{(i_j - i_{j-1})!} \lim_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{P}\left[ E_N \cap E_N^4 \right] \notag\\ &\phantom{\geq} - \sum_{\substack{i_1\leq \dots\leq i_{k-1}\\ \in \{0,\dots,k\} : i_j \geq j}} \sum_{\mathcal{I} \subset [k]} \lim_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{E} \Bigg[ c_N(\tau_N(t_{j^*(I)-1})) + \sum_{s=\tau_N(t_{j^\star(\mathcal{I}) -1})+1}^{\tau_N(t_{j^\star(\mathcal{I}) })} c_N(s)^2 \Bigg] ( t+2 )^{2k} \notag\\ &= \sum_{\substack{i_1\leq \dots\leq i_{k-1}\\ \in \{0,\dots,k\} : i_j \geq j}} \prod_{j=1}^k \frac{(t_j - t_{j-1})^{i_j - i_{j-1}}}{(i_j - i_{j-1})!}, \end{align*} where we used \eqref{eq:BJJK_eq3.3} and \eqref{eq:BJJK_eq3.5} to conclude that the sum in the expectation vanishes, and Lemmata \ref{thm:lim_AandB}, \ref{thm:indicators_cN}, and \ref{thm:indicators_c2} to obtain that $\lim_{N\to\infty}\mathbb{P}[E_N \cap E_N^4] =1$. The upper and lower bounds coincide, so the proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Lower limit matches upper

nodes.name: Intersection of high-probability events
nodes.statement: {\cite[Lemma 4.11]{brown2021thesis}} Let $(A_N) , (B_N)$ be sequences of events. If $\lim_{N\to\infty}\mathbb{P}[A_N] = \lim_{N\to\infty}\mathbb{P}[B_N]=1$ then $\lim_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{P} [A_N \cap B_N] =1$.
nodes.label: thm:lim_AandB

nodes.name: Indicator lemma for c_N bounded
nodes.statement: Assume \eqref{eq:BJJK_eq3.5} holds. Fix $t>0$. Let $K_N>0$ be a sequence independent of $r$ and bounded away from 0. Define $E_N(r) := \{ c_N(r) < K_N \}$ and $E_N := \bigcap_{r=1}^{\tau_N(t)} E_N(r)$. Then $\lim_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{P}[E_N]=1$.
nodes.origin_citation: Brown 2021 (thesis), Lemmata 4.12-4.14; variants of Koskela et al. 2022, Supplement Lemma 4
nodes.statement_short: c_N(r) stays below a level bounded away from 0 up to tau_N(t) w.p. -> 1.
assumptions: $K_N>0$ be a sequence independent of $r$ and bounded away from 0
nodes.label: thm:indicators_cN

nodes.name: Indicator lemma for tau_N
nodes.statement: Assume \eqref{eq:BJJK_eq3.5} holds. Fix $t > 0$. For any $l \in \mathbb{N}$, $\mathbb{P}[ \tau_N(t) \geq l ] \to 1$ as $N \to \infty$.
nodes.origin_citation: Brown 2021 (thesis), Lemmata 4.12-4.14; variants of Koskela et al. 2022, Supplement Lemma 4
nodes.statement_short: tau_N(t) >= l with probability tending to 1.
nodes.label: thm:indicators_tau

nodes.name: Indicator lemma for c_N dominating D_N
nodes.statement: Assume \eqref{eq:BJJK_eq3.4} holds. Fix $t>0$. Let $K$ be a constant not depending on $N$ or $r$. Then \begin{equation*} \lim_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{P} \Bigg[ \bigcap_{r=1}^{\tau_N(t)} \left\{ c_N(r) \geq K D_N(r) \right\} \Bigg] = 1 . \end{equation*}
nodes.origin_citation: Brown 2021 (thesis), Lemmata 4.12-4.14; variants of Koskela et al. 2022, Supplement Lemma 4
nodes.statement_short: c_N(r) >= K D_N(r) for all r <= tau_N(t) w.p. -> 1.
assumptions: $K$ be a constant not depending on $N$ or $r$
nodes.label: thm:indicators_DN

nodes.name: Indicator lemma for sums of squared c_N
nodes.statement: Assume \eqref{eq:BJJK_eq3.5} holds. Fix $k\in\mathbb{N}$, a sequence of times $0 = t_0 \leq t_1 \leq \cdots \leq t_k \leq t$, and let $K_{ 1 : k }$ be strictly positive constants. Define the event \begin{equation*} E_N := \bigcap_{j=1}^k \Bigg\{ \sum_{s=\tau_N(t_{j-1})+1}^{\tau_N(t_j)} c_N(s)^2 \leq K_j \Bigg\} . \end{equation*} Then $\lim_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{P}[E_N] =1$.
nodes.statement_short: Sums of c_N^2 over each interval stay below given positive constants w.p. -> 1.
nodes.label: thm:indicators_c2

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 15
nodes.statement: \begin{align*} \mathbb{P}[E_N] &= 1- \mathbb{P}[E_N^c] = 1- \mathbb{P}\Bigg[ \bigcup_{j=1}^k \Bigg\{ \sum_{s=\tau_N(t_{j-1})+1} ^{\tau_N(t_j)} c_N(s)^2 > K_j \Bigg\} \Bigg] \\ &\geq 1- \sum_{j=1}^k \mathbb{P}\Bigg[ \sum_{s=\tau_N(t_{j-1})+1} ^{\tau_N(t_j)} c_N(s)^2 \geq K_j \Bigg] . \end{align*} Applying Markov's inequality and using \eqref{eq:BJJK_eq3.5} gives \begin{equation*} \mathbb{P}[E_N] \geq 1- \sum_{j=1}^k K_j^{-1} \mathbb{E}\Bigg[ \sum_{s=\tau_N(t_{j-1})+1} ^{\tau_N(t_j)} c_N(s)^2 \Bigg] \underset{N\to\infty}{\longrightarrow} 1- \sum_{j=1}^k K_j^{-1} \times 0 = 1, \end{equation*} as required.
nodes.statement_short: Union bound plus Markov's inequality and (15).

nodes.name: Fubini and dominated convergence conditions
nodes.statement: For any fixed $t>0$, for $N$ sufficiently large, \begin{equation*} \mathbb{E} \Bigg[ \sum_{l=0}^\infty \Big| (-\alpha_n)^l 1_N \frac{1}{l!} t^l \sum_{\substack{r_1 < \cdots < r_k : \\ r_i \leq \tau_N(t_i) \forall i}} \prod_{i=1}^k c_N(r_i) \Big| \Bigg] < \infty . \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: The expected absolute series in the expansion is finite, justifying exchange of limit, expectation and sum.
nodes.label: thm:DCT_Fubini
